किनांक 01.01.2020 से 30.07.2025 की अिर्ध क े  िौरान, प्रितिन र्निेशालय ने धन-शोधन र्निारण 
अर्धर्नयम, 2002 (पीएमएलए) क े प्रािधानों क े  तहत धन शोधन क े  अपराध से िुडे लगभग 220 
मामलों में िााँच संबंधी कारििाई शुरू की है।   
728                                                      

ितिमान में भारत में किप्टो आजस्तयां विर्नयर्मत नह़ीं हैं। भारतीय ररज़िि बैंक-सचेत पोटिल पर 
अपंिीकृत/ अर्नगर्मत र्नकायों से अनर्धकृत िमा गर्तविर्धयों से संबंर्धत र्शकायतें प्राप्त होती हैं। 
किनांक 1 अप्रैल, 2020 से 31 माचि, 2025 क े  िौरान, सचेत पोटिल पर 'विर्भन्न प्रकार की र्निेश 
योिनाओं से एकवत्रत धन का पुनभुिगतान न करने' से संबंर्धत लगभग 3,454 र्शक ायतें प्राप्त हुई हैं, 
और र्शकायतकतािओं द्वारा चयर्नत र्शकायत श्रेजणयों क े  आधार पर, 'एमएलएम, डायरेक्ट सेर्लंग और 
पोंिी योिनाओं क े  माध्यम से धन उगाह़ी' से संबंर्धत 1,531 र्शक ायतें प्राप्त हुई हैं।  
इस तरह की धोखाधड़ी को रोकने , उसका पता लगाने और उसक े  विरुि का रििाई करने क े  र्लए कई 
पहलें की गई हैं  और र्निेशक िागरूकता अर्भयान चलाए िा रहे हैं, िो इस प्रकार हैं:  
(i) गृह मंत्रालय (एमएचए) द्वारा स्थावपत भारतीय साइबर अपराध समन्िय क ें द्र (आई4सी) में साइबर 
धोखाधड़ी प्रशमन क ेंद्र (सीएफएमसी) और 'सस् पेक् ट रजिस्ऱी' की स् थापना की गई है जिसमें प्रमुख 
वित्तीय संस्थानों, िूरसंचार सेिा प्रिाताओं, आईट़ी मध्यस्थों और राज्यों/संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों की विर्ध 
प्रितिन एिेंर्सयों क े  प्रर्तर्नर्ध शार्मल हैं तथा इसक े  साथ ह़ी गृह मंत्रालय (एमएचए) द्वारा गकठत एक 
िररष्ठ स्तऱीय समन्िय समूह (एसएलसीिी) भी साइबर धोखाधड़ी से संबंर्धत मुद्दों का समाधान करता 
है। 
(ii)  भारतीय ररििि बैंक ने कडजिटल लैंकडग एप् लीक े शन द्वारा अनैर्तक पिर्तयों से संबंर्धत मुद्दों का 
समाधान करने क े  र्लए भारतीय ररज़िि बैंक (कडजिटल ऋण) किशार्निेश, 2025 िाऱी ककए हैं और 
साइबर धोखाधड़ी और मनी म्यूल गर्तविर्ध का पता लगाने हेतु सुदृढ़ प्रणार्लयों को अपनाने क े र्लए 
बैंकों को गोपनीय एडिाइिऱी िाऱी की है। 
(iii)  भारतीय ररििि बैंक धोखाधड़ी क े  विर्भन् न प्रकारों और र्निारण तंत्रों क े  संबंध में उपभोक्ताओं को 
िागरूक करने क े  र्लए ट़ीिी, वप्रंट, एसएमएस और कडजिटल प्लेटफॉमि िैसे कक  आरबीआई कहता है 
अर्भयान और बी(ए)िेयर' पुजस्तका क े  माध्यम से सुरजक्षत कडजिटल कायिप्रणार्लयों क े  बारे में िन 
िागरूकता पैिा करता है।  
(iv)  वित्त िर्षि 2024-25 में, सेबी ने एसोर्सएशन ऑफ म्यूचुअल फंड्स इन इंकडया (एएमएफआई) और 
एसेट मैनेिमेंट कंपनीि (एएमसी) क े  साथ र्मलकर 36 राज्यों और संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों क े  724 जिलों 
में र्निेशक िागरूकता कायििम आयोजित ककए , जिनमें लगभग 32 लाख र्निेशकों को किर ककया 
गया। सेबी ने र्निेशकों की सु रक्षा क े र्लए शैक्षजणक संसाधन और र्निेश संबंधी िानकाऱी प्रिान 
करने िाला Saa₹thi मोबाइल ऐप भी लॉन्च ककया है।  
(v) सेबी "सेबी बनाम स् कैम" अर्भयान चलाता है, िो बािार अिसंरचना संस् थानों (एमआईआई) क े  
साथ र्मलकर ट़ीिी, वप्रंट, रेकडयो और सोशल मीकडया क े  माध्यम से धोखाधड़ी क े  बारे में िागरूकता 
अर्भयान चलाता है।

(क ) व्यापाररक पररचालन पुनः आरंभ करने क े  प्रयासों में कलकत्ता स्टॉक एक्सचेंि की ितिमान

या जबना आपूजतग के चालान िारी  जकया िाता है, या अजिक आईटीसी प्राप्त/जवतररत  जकया 
िाता है, अब िंि का भागी   होगा।  
• इनवॉइस प्रबंिन प्रणाली (आईएमएस) को िीएसटी पोटगल पर  2024 के अंत में शुरू  जकया 
गया  है, जिसका उद्देश्य प्राप्तकतागओं को प्राप्त चालानों के प्रभावी प्रबंिन में मिि करना  है। 
यह प्रणाली प्राप्तकतागओं को चालानों को स्वीकार करने , अस्वीकार करने  या लंजबत जचजित 
करने  की सुजविा िेती है, िब उन्ें आपूजतगकताग द्वारा सहेिा या िाखखल  जकया गया  हो। इसक े 
माध्यम से प्राप्तकताग आपूजतगकताग द्वारा िीएसटीआर  -1 में ििग चालानों का जमलान और  
सत्यापन करक े  आईटीसी िावे की प्रजक्रया को सरल  और  सुदृढ़ बना सकते हैं।

(ख)  िर्षष 2020-21 को छोडकर, िास्तविक प्रत्यक्ष कर संग्रह बजट अनुमानों से अवधक रहा। यह उल्लेख करना 
प्रासंवगक होगा वक िर्षष 2020-21 एक कोविड िर्षष था। िर्षष 2020-21 में, राजकोर्षीय घाटा 9.2% था, 
जबवक बजट अनुमान सकल घरेलू उत्पाि का 3.5% था। िर्षष 2020-21 में प्रमुख सािषजवनक व्यय 
कायषिमों को वियाप्तित करने की सरकार की क्षमता प्रभावित नहीं हुई क्योंवक सरकार ने महामारी से 
उत्पन्न चुनौवतयों का सामना वकया और वनयवमत अंतराल पर प्रधानमंत्री गरीब कल्याण स्कीम जैसी 
योजनाओं क े  माध्यम से आवथषक पैक े जों की घोर्षणा की।

II. कनधाषररती ओां ि े  कलए अनुपालन में आसानी 
(i) पूांजीगत लाभ िराधान व्यवस्था िा सरलीिरण और युक्तििरण : संशोवधत प्रािधानों क े  साथ 
पूंजीगत पररसंपवत्तयों को धारण करने की अिवध को सरल बनाया गया है , वजसमें पूंजीगत पररसंपवत्तयों क े  
वलए 12/24 महीने की धारण अिवध प्रिान की गई है। इस अवधवनयम की धारा 111ए क े  तहत 
अिकावलक पूंजीगत लाभ पर कर की िर एसटीटी भुगतान िाले सूचीबद्ध इप्तिटी शेयरों, इप्तिटी-उन्मुख 
फ ं डों की इकाइयों और व्यािसावयक ट र स्टों क े  वलए 15% से बढ़ाकर 20% कर िी गई है। उपरोक्त पूंजीगत 
पररसंपवत्तयों पर िीघषकावलक पूंजीगत लाभ की िर को 10% से युप्तक्तसंगत बनाकर 12.5% कर विया गया 
है। अन्य िीघषकावलक पूंजीगत पररसंपवत्तयों क े  संबंध में कराधान की िर को युप्तक्तसंगत और सरल बनाकर

(i) िकतपय निद कनिासी पर टीडीएस िा प्रावधान - वित्त (संख्या 2) अवधवनयम, 2019 ने बैंक/डाकघर

प्रािधान करने क े  वलए अवधवनयम में धारा 194एन जोडी है। ररटनष िाप्तखल करना सुवनवित करने और ररटनष 
न भरने िालों द्वारा नकि वनकासी पर नज़र रखने क े  वलए, वित्त अवधवनयम, 2020 ने नकि वनकासी की 
सीमा को घटाकर 20 लाख रुपये कर विया और इन ररटनष न भरने िालों द्वारा 1 करोड रुपये से अवधक की 
नकि वनकासी पर 5% की उच्च िर से टीडीएस काटना भी अवनिायष कर विया। वित्त अवधवनयम, 2023 ने 
सहकारी सवमवतयों को 1 करोड रुपये की क ु ल नकि वनकासी की सीमा को बढ़ाकर 3 करोड रुपये करक े  
राहत प्रिान की है । 
 
(ii) कडकजटल लेनदेन िो बढावा - छोटे व्यिसायों क े  वलए प्रकप्तित योजना क े  तहत वडवजटल टनषओिर क े  
संबंध में पहले से मौजूि लाभ की िर 8% से घटाकर 6% कर िी गई थी। उन व्यप्तक्तयों क े  वलए जो अपने 
95% लेनिेन वडवजटल रूप से कर रहे हैं , कर लेखापरीक्षा क े  टनषओिर की सीमा को बढ़ाकर 10 करोड 
रुपये कर विया गया है। वित्त अवधवनयम, 2023 ने कवतपय शतों क े  अधीन कराधान की प्रकप्तित योजना 
का लाभ उठाने क े  वलए प्रारंवभक सीमा बढ़ा िी है। छोटे उद्यमों वजनकी नकि प्राप्तियां 5 प्रवतशत से 
अवधक नहीं हैं, प्रकप्तित योजना का लाभ उठाने की सीमा 2 करोड रुपये से बढ़ाकर 3 करोड रुपये कर 
िी गई है। ऐसे पेशेिरों क े  मामले में वजनकी नकि प्राप्तियां 5 प्रवतशत से अवधक नहीं हैं, उनक े  वलए उक्त 
सीमा 50 लाख रुपये से बढ़ाकर 75 लाख रुपये कर िी गई है।

(iii) भुगतान ि े  कनधाषररत इलेक्ट् र ॉकनि तरीि े  ि े  कलए अकनवायष सुकवधा - यह प्रािधान वकया गया

इलेक्ट र ॉवनक तरीकों क े  माध्यम से भुगतान स्वीकार करने की सुविधा प्रिान करनी होगी, वजस पर 
कोई एमडीआर शुल्क नहीं वलया जाएगा। 
 
(iv) निद लेन-देन पर प्रकतबांध- इस अवधवनयम की धारा 269एसटी क े  अंतगषत इलेक्ट र ॉवनक माध्यमों

लगा विया गया है। धमाषथष संगठनों को नकि िान की सीमा 10,000 रुपये से घटाकर 2,000 रुपये

प्रवतबंवधत कर विया गया है। नकि व्यािसावयक व्यय की सीमा 20,000 रुपये से घटाकर 10,000 
रुपये कर िी गई है।  
V. िर अपवांचन रोिने और िर आधार बढाने ि े  कलए किए गए उपाय  
(i) पैन िा उल्लेख िरना और पैन िो आधार से जोड़ना अकनवायष िर कदया गया है - पैन का उल्लेख 
करना अवनिायष कर विया गया है और पैन और आधार को जोडना भी अवनिायष कर विया गया है।  
 
(ii) िाला धन अकधकनयम- वििेशों में जमा काले धन क े  प्रिाह को रोकने क े  वलए काला धन (अघोवर्षत वििेशी

गया है। 
 
(iii) बेनामी िानून- बेनामी संपवत्त को जब्त करने और बेनामीिार और लाभाथी स्वामी क े  प्तखलाफ मुकिमा 
चलाने क े  वलए बेनामी लेनिेन (वनर्षेध) अवधवनयम, 1988 को बेनामी लेनिेन (वनर्षेध) संशोधन अवधवनयम, 
2016 द्वारा व्यापक रूप से संशोवधत वकया गया था।

2. कनवेश और रोजगार िो बढावा देने ि े  उपाय –– 
 
2.1. आईएफएससी िो प्रोत्साहन –– 
कवत्त अकधकनयम, 2025 ने आईएफएससी िो कनम्नकलक्तखत प्रोत्साहन प्रदान किए हैं - 
 अवधवनयम की विवभन्न धाराओं अथाषत धारा 80एलए (2) (घ), धारा 10 (4घ), धारा 10 (4च), धारा (4ज) और 
धारा 47 (vii एडी) में छ ू ट, कटौती और रीलोक े शन क े  वलए आईएफएससी इकाइयों से संबंवधत सनसेट 
वतवथयों को 31 माचष, 2030 तक बढ़ा विया गया है। 
 आईएफएससी बीमा मध्यस्थ कायाषलय द्वारा जारी जीिन बीमा पॉवलसी पर प्राि आय को धारा 10(10घ) के 
प्रािधानों में वनविषष्ट् प्रीवमयम रावश पर वकसी भी शतष क े  वबना छ ू ट िी जाएगी। 
 धारा 10(4ज) में छ ू ट को पट्टे पर जहाज िेने िाली घरेलू क ं पनी क े  इप्तिटी शेयरों क े  हस्तांतरण पर 
अवनिासी या आईएफएससी की एक इकाई क े  वलए क ै वपटल गेन्स तक बढ़ाया जाएगा। 
 िो समूह संस्थाओं क े  बीच कोई भी अवग्रम या ऋण, जहां समूह की एक संस्था आईएफएससी में राजकोर्षीय 
गवतविवधयों या राजकोर्षीय सेिाओं क े  वलए स्थावपत है, को लाभांश से बाहर रखा जाएगा।  
 आईएफएससी प्तस्थत फ ं ड मैनेजर द्वारा प्रबंवधत वनिेश वनवधयों क े  वलए धारा 9ए में एक सरलीक ृ त सुरवक्षत 
बंिरगाह व्यिस्था प्रिान की गई है। आईएफएससी इकाइयों क े  वलए शतों में छ ू ट 31 माचष, 2030 तक शुरू 
होने िाली इकाइयों क े  वलए बढ़ा िी गई है। 
 धारा 10(4ङ) क े  तहत छ ू ट वकसी भी वििेशी पोटषफोवलयो वनिेशक, अथाषत भारतीय प्रवतभूवत और विवनमय 
बोडष (वििेशी पोटषफोवलयो वनिेशक) विवनयम, 2014 क े  प्रािधानों क े  अनुसार पंजीक ृ त व्यप्तक्त क े  साथ वकए 
गए गैर -वडलीिरी योग्य अवग्रम अनुबंधों या ओडीआई या ओटीसी क े  हस्तांतरण या ओडीआई पर आय क े  
वितरण क े  पररणामस्वरूप वकसी अवनिासी को प्राि या प्राि होने िाली वकसी भी आय पर लागू होती है। 
 इसक े  अलािा अवधवनयम की धारा 10(4घ) में वनविषष्ट् खुिरा योजना या एक्सचेंज ट रेडेड फ ं ड (ईटीएफ) क े

2.3. इलेक्ट् र ॉकनक्स कवकनमाषण सुकवधा ि े  कलए सेवाए ां  प्रदान िरने वाले अकनवासी ि े  कलए प्रिक्तित

सामान, िस्तु या चीज क े  विवनमाषण या उत्पािन क े  वलए इलेक्ट र ॉवनक्स विवनमाषण सुविधा या संबद्ध सुविधा 
स्थावपत या संचावलत करने िाली वनिासी क ं पनी को प्रौद्योवगकी क े  प्रािधान सवहत सेिाए ं  प्रिान करने क े

2.4. अांतदेशीय जहाजोां ि े  कलए टन भार िर योजना ि े  लाभोां िा कवस्तार ––

3. सरलीिरण और युक्तििरण –– 
 
3.1. आयिर कवधेयि, 2025 िा पररचय : 
सरकार ने आयकर अवधवनयम , 1961 (अवधवनयम) की व्यापक समीक्षा की घोर्षणा की है। उक्त समीक्षा क े  
पररणामस्वरूप , आयकर विधेयक , 2025 (2025 का विधेयक संख्या 24) विनांक 13.02.2025 को 
लोकसभा में प्रस्तुत वकया गया है और इसे जांच हेतु लोकसभा की प्रिर सवमवत को भेजा गया है। 
आयकर विधेयक को प्रस्तुत करने का उद्देश्य मौजूिा आयकर अवधवनयम, 1961 को संवक्षि, सुबोध, 
पठनीय और समझने में आसान बनाकर उसे सरल बनाना था। सरलीकरण की यह प्रविया तीन प्रमुख 
वसद्धांतों पर आधाररत थी: - 
1. बेहतर स्पष्ट्ता और सुसंगतता क े  वलए पा्य  और संरचनात्मक सरलीकरण। 
2. वनरंतरता और वनवितता सुवनवित करने क े  वलए कर कोई बडा कर नीवत पररितषन  नहीं वकया 
जाएगा। 
3. कर िरों में कोई संशोधन नहीं , वनधाषररती ओं क े  वलए पूिाषनुमान को बनाए रखना 
 
इस उद्देश्य क े  वलए तीन-आयामी दृवष्ट्कोण अपनाया गया: - 
 
1. पठनीयता बढ़ाने क े  वलए जवटल भार्षा को हटाना। 
2. बेहतर नेविगेशन क े  वलए अनािश्यक और िोहराि िाले प्रािधानों को हटाना। 
3. संिभष को आसान बनाने क े  वलए धाराओं  को तावक ष क रूप से पुनगषवठत करना।  
 
सरलीकरण की प्रविया शुरू करते समय , अनजाने में होने िाली अस्पष्ट्ता, वजससे नई व्याख्याए ाँ  और 
मुकिमेबाज़ी की संभािना कम से कम हो, क े  वलए सचेत प्रयास वकए गए हैं। इस उद्देश्य क े  वलए, अन्य 
बातों क े  अलािा, वनम्नवलप्तखत उपाय वकए गए हैं: 
क.  मुख्य शब्ों/िाक्यांशों को, विशेर्षकर जहां न्यायालयों ने वनणषय विए हैं, न्यूनतम संशोधनों 
क े  साथ बरकरार रखा गया है , तथा छोटे िाक्यों क े  प्रयोग द्वारा भार्षा को सरल बनाया गया है। 
ख.  बहु व्याख्याओं की संभािना को कम करने क े  वलए प्रािधान स्पष्ट् कर विए गए हैं। 
प्रािधानों और स्पष्ट्ीकरणों को हटा विया गया है और सरलीक ृ त विर्षय-िस्तु को उप-धाराओं 
और खंडों क े  रूप में रखा गया है।  
ग.  स्पष्ट्ता बढ़ाने क े  वलए सूत्रों और तावलकाओं का उपयोग वकया गया है। 
घ.  समान मुद्दों तथा पररभार्षाओं िाले प्रािधान में जो मौजूिा अवधवनयम क े  अलग -
अलगअध्याओं में थे उन प्रािधान को समेवकत वकया गया है। 
इस प्रकार आयकर विधेयक , 2025, सरल , स्पष्ट् और शुद्ध कर ढांचा प्रिान करक े  व्यापार करने में 
आसानी बढ़ाने क े  वलए सरकार की प्रवतबद्धता को िशाषता है। 
3.2. िकतपय टीडीएस दरोां िा युक्तििरण –– 
िरों की बहुलता और अनुपालन  के भार को कम करने क े  वलए , कवतपय टीडीएस और टीसीएस िरों को 
कम वकया गया है , जबवक स्रोत पर कर कटौती या स्रोत पर कर संग्रह की आिश्यकता क े  वलए कवतपय 
सीमाए ाँ  बढ़ा िी गई हैं। इसक े  अलािा, अवधवनयम की धारा 206सी(1ज) को लागू नहीं वकया गया है। 
 
3.3. धमाषथष ट र स्ट/सांस्थाए ँ  –– 
छोटे ट र स्टों या संस्थाओं क े  वलए ट र स्ट या संस्था क े  पंजीकरण की िैधता अिवध 5 िर्षष से बढ़ाकर 10 िर्षष 
करने हेतु संशोधन वकए गए हैं। ट र स्ट या संस्था क े  पंजीकरण को रद्द करने क े  वलए वनविषष्ट् उल्लंघन की 
परर भार्षा को युप्तक्तसंगत बनाया गया है तावक इसे अपूणष आिेिनों क े  रूप में मामूली चूक क े  वलए लागू न 
वकया जाए। इसक े  अलािा, छ ू ट से इनकार करने क े  वलए वकसी ट र स्ट या संस्था को पयाषि योगिान िेने िाले 
व्यप्तक्तयों की पररभार्षा को भी युप्तक्तसंगत बनाया गया है । 
754                                                      

 
3.4. 'पूांजीगत पररसांपकत्त' िी पररभाषा में सांशोधन –– 
पूंजीगत पररसंपवत्त की पररभार्षा में संशोधन वकया गया है , वजसमें श्रेणी I या श्रेणी II िैकप्तिक वनिेश वनवध 
क े  रूप में मान्यता प्राि और भारतीय प्रवतभूवत और विवनमय बोडष (िैकप्तिक वनिेश वनवध) विवनयम, 
2012 के  तहत विवनयवमत या अंतर ाषष्ट्र ीय वित्तीय सेिा कें द्र प्रावधकर ण (वनवध प्रबंधन) विवनयम, 2022 क े  
तहत विवनयवमत वकसी वनिेश वनवध द्वारा रखी गई कोई भी प्रवतभूवत शावमल है, वजसने भारतीय प्रवतभूवत 
और विवनमय बोडष अवधवनयम , 1992 या आईएफएससीए अवधवनयम, 2019 क े  तहत बनाए गए विवनयमों 
क े  अनुसार ऐसी प्रवतभूवतयों में वनिेश वकया है। 
 
3.5. स्टाटष-अप्स िे कलए िर लाभ िी समय-सीमा िा कवस्तार –– 
इस अवधवनयम में संशोधन करक े  धारा 80-झग क े  अंतगषत स्टाटषअप्स को प्रिान वकए जाने िाले लाभ को 
पांच िर्षष की अवतररक्त अिवध क े  वलए बढ़ा विया गया है, अथाषत यह लाभ  विनांक 01.04.2030 से पहले 
वनगवमत पात्र स्टाटषअप्स को उपलब्ध होगा। 
 
3.6. बहु-वषीय आर्म्ष लेंथ मूल् कनधाषरण ि े  कलए स्थानाांतरण मूल् कनधाषरण प्रावधानोां िा युक्तििरण –
– 
इस अवधवनयम में संशोधन वकया गया है , तावक समान लेनिेन क े  संबंध में मूल्य वनधाषरण हेतु हस्तांतरण 
मूल्य वनधाषरण प्रािधान अब 3 िर्षष की अिवध क े  वलए लागू हों। 
 
4. िर प्रशासन –– 
 
4.1. कक्रप्टो-पररसांपकत्त ि े  सांबांध में सूचना प्रस्तुत िरने िा दाकयत्व –– 
इस अवधवनयम में धारा 285खकक को शावमल वकया गया है, जो इसमें वनधाषररत संस्थाओं क े  वलए वनधाषररत 
वनयमों क े  अनुसार विप्टो-पररसंपवत्तयों की जानकारी प्रिान करने का िावयत्व है। इसक े  अवतररक्त, इस 
अवधवनयम की धारा 2 क े  खंड (47क) में आभासी वडवजटल पररसंपवत्त की पररभार्षा को संशोवधत करक े  
यह कहा गया है वक आभासी वडवजटल पररसंपवत्त में सीएआरएफ  क े  तहत िी गई पररभार्षा क े  अनुसार 
कोई भी विप्टो-पररसंपवत्त शावमल है। 
 
4.2. अद्यतन ररटनष दाक्तखल िरने िी समय-सीमा बढाना- 
अद्यतन ररटनष िाप्तखल करने की समय-सीमा को संबंवधत कर वनधाषरण िर्षष की समाप्ति से मौजूिा 24 
महीने से बढ़ाकर 48 महीने कर विया गया है।

(क)  मंत्रािय न े राज्यों में गुणव त्तापूणा उत्पादों क ी स्थापन ा सुनन श्चचत क रन े के लिए, हदनांक 11 फ़रवरी 2025 
को 'तापीय ऊर्ाा भंडारण बैकअप सहहत सौर कोल्ड स्टोरेर् प्रणालियों के डडजाइन, प्रदशान और परीक्षण 
मानकों ' पर एक  व्यापक  हदशानन देश अधध सूधचत कक या है। मंत्रािय, सौर कोल्ड भंडारण  सहहत सभी नवीकरणीय

(ख ) अब तक ऐसी ककसी  साझेदारी की संभावना नहीं तिाशी  गई है।  
(ग) अभी तक  ऐसा क ोई उपाय िागू न हीं कक या गया है। तथावप, सौर ऊर्ाा उपकरणों, ववशेष रूप से सौर पीवी

(क )  िेश में अब तक राज्य-र्ार ककतने पेट्रोक े वमकल हब स्थावपत ककए गए हैं; 
(ख)  आगामी किनों में राज्य-र्ार ककतने पेट्रोक े वमकल हब स्थावपत ककए जाने का प्रस्तार् है; और  
(ग)  पेट्रोक े वमकल क्षेत्र में कायवनीवतक रूप से महत्र्पूर्व क्षेत्रों, वजन्हें एफडीआई से 100 प्रवतशत छूट

सक े  एर्ं रोज़गार सृजन ककया जा सक े । पीसीपीआईआर , व्यर्साय स्थावपत करने क े  वलए अनुक ू ल 
प्रवतस्पिी र्ातार्रर् प्रिान करने हेतु साझा अर्संरिना और सहायक सेर्ाओं क े साथ वर्कास क े  एक 
क्लस्टर-आिाररत मॉडल पर आिा ररत हैं।  
इन क्षेत्रों में वनर्ेश तथा औद्योवगक वर्कास को बढार्ा िेने क े  वलए आंध्र प्रिेश (वर्शाखापत्तनम), गुजरात 
(िाहेज) और ओवडशा (पारािीप) राज्यों में  तीन पेट्रोवलयम, रसायन और पेट्रोरसायन वनर्ेश क्षेत्र 
(पीसीपीआईआर) अविसूवित ककए गए हैं।  
(ख) र्तवमान में, ऐसा कोई प्रस्तार् वर्भाग में वर्िारािीन नहीं है। 
(ग) सामान्यतः पेट्रोरसायन क्षेत्र 100% एफडीआई क े  वलए खुला है , वजसमें क ु छ खतरनाक रसायन 
शावमल नहीं  हैं, वजनक े  वलए अवनर्ायव लाइसेंससंग की आर्श्यकता होती है।

(क):  सागरमाला कायᭅᮓम क े  तहत कायाᭅ᭠ वयन हेतु 5.79 लाख करोड़ ᱧ. क े िनवेश कᳱ 839 पᳯरयोजनाएं

᳇ारा कायाᭅि᭠वत कᳱ जाती हᱹ। इनमᱶ से 1.42 लाख करोड़ ᱧ. कᳱ लागत कᳱ 280 पᳯरयोजनाएं पूरी हो गई 
हᱹ, और 1.62 लाख करोड़ ᱧ. कᳱ 209 पᳯरयोजनाएं कायाᭅ᭠ वयनाधीन है। इसके अितᳯर᭍ त, 2.75 लाख 
करोड़ ᱧ. कᳱ 350 पᳯरयोजनाएं िवकास के िविभ᭠ न चरणᲂ मᱶ है।  
 
(ख): सागरमाला कायᭅᮓम के तहत पᳯरयोजना क े  कायाᭅ᭠ वयन मᱶ िवलंब मु᭎ यत: भूिम अिधᮕहण, वैधािनक 
िनकािसयᲂ मᱶ िवलंब, ᭭ थानीय आंदोलन, कायᭅᭃेᮢ मᱶ पᳯरवतᭅन के कारण होता है। अवसंरचना 
पᳯरयोजनाᲐ का  िबना िवलंब क े पूरा ᳰकया जाना सुिनि᳟त करने हेतु उठाए गए ᮧमुख कदम मᱶ, मंᮢालय 
मᱶ िविभ᭠ न ᭭ तरᲂ पर पᳯरयोजनाᲐ  कᳱ आविधक समीᭃा, ᭪ यवि᭭थत पᳯरयोजना मू᭨ यांकन और िवᱫपोषण 
ᳰदशा- िनदᱷश शािमल है। मंᮢालय समय- समय पर मैरीटाइम रा᭔ य िवकास पᳯरषद (एमएसडीसी) कᳱ

भतᱮ और िनयुिᲦ कᳱ िनगरानी कᳱ जा रही है।  
iii. वािण᭔ य पोत पᳯरवहन (समुᮤी ᮰िमक) िनयम, 2016 क े  अंतगᭅत पोतᲂ पर कायᭅरत नािवकᲂ के 
िलए ᮰म मानकᲂ  कᳱ िनगरानी कᳱ जा रही है।  
iv. ई-ᮧवास ᮧणाली और आᮯजन ᭣यूरो क े  साथ नौवहन महािनदेशालय (डीजी िशᳲपग) ᳇ारा उठाए 
गए कदमᲂ क े  मा᭟यम से िवदेशᲂ मᱶ िनयोिजत नािवकᲂ कᳱ िनगरानी कᳱ जा रही है।  
v. भारतीय नािवकᲂ कᳱ आसानी से पहचान करने क े  िलए बायोमेᳯᮝक नािवक पहचान द᭭तावेज 
(बीएसआईडी) शुᱨ ᳰकया गया।     
vi. नािवकᲂ को आसानी से सीडीसी जारी करने हेतु वािण᭔य पोत पᳯरवहन (सीडीसी) िनयम, 2017 
को अिधसूिचत ᳰकया गया।  
vii. िशकायत कᳱ उिचत फाइᳲलग और िनगरानी क े  िलए ऑनलाइन िशकायत िनगरानी ᮧणाली 
᭭थािपत कᳱ गई है।

भारत सरकार 
पᱫन, पोत पᳯरवहन और जलमागᭅ मंᮢालय 
 
रा᭔ य सभा 
 
अतारांᳰकत ᮧ᳤ सं. 1914 िजसका उᱫर 
मंगलवार, 5 अग᭭ त, 2025 (14 ᮰ावण, 1947,(शक)) को ᳰदया जाना है 
 
भारतीय पᱫनᲂ ᳇ारा संचािलत समुᮤी ᳞ ापार 
 
1914 ᮰ी सतनाम ᳲसंह संधू :   
 
᭍या पᱫन पोत पᳯरवहन और जलमागᭅ मंᮢी यह बताने कᳱ क ृ पा करᱶगे ᳰकः 
 
(क) िवगत पाँच वषᲄ मᱶ भारतीय पᱫनᲂ ᳇ारा संचािलत समुᮤी ᳞ ापार कᳱ क ु ल माᮢा, िजसमᱶ समुᮤी मागᲄ 
क े  मा᭟यम से ᳰकए गए िनयाᭅत और आयात का ᮧितशत भी शािमल है, ᳰकतनी है; 
(ख) ᭍या सरकार ने भारत मᱶ जहाज िनमाᭅण उ᳒ोग को बढ़ावा देने और िवदेशी िनᳶमᭅत जहाजᲂ पर 
िनभᭅरता कम करने के  िलए कदम उठाए हᱹ और यᳰद हाँ, तो त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या है; 
(ग) घरेलू जहाज िनमाᭅण और मर᭥मत सुिवधाᲐ को बढ़ावा देने के िलए मैरीटाइम इंिडया िवजन 2030 क े 
अंतगᭅत ᮧदान ᳰकए गए ᮧो᭜साहनᲂ का ᭣यौरा ᭍या है; 
(घ) देश के तटीय पोत पᳯरवहन ᭃेᮢ कᳱ वतᭅमान ि᭭थित ᭍या है; और 
(ङ) देश क े  तटीय और ᮧमुख पोत पᳯरवहन मागᲄ पर समुᮤी सुरᭃा बढ़ाने और िनगरानी को मजबूत करने 
क े  िलए ᭍या उपाय ᳰकए गए हᱹ?

932                                                      

(ख) और (ग): मैरीटाइम इंिडया िवज़न 2030 के अंतगᭅत, सरकार ने भारत मᱶ पोत िनमाᭅण उ᳒ोग को 
बढ़ावा देने और िवदेशी िनᳶमᭅत पोतᲂ पर िनभᭅरता कम करने क े  िलए कई कदम उठाए हᱹ, जो इस ᮧकार हᱹ:- 
(i) मंᮢालय ने पोत िनमाᭅण गितिविधयᲂ मᱶ और अिधक भागीदारी को ᮧो᭜सािहत करने क े  िलए 
29.01.2025 को पोत िनमाᭅण िवᱫीय सहायता नीित (एसबीएफएपी) ᳰदशा-िनदᱷशᲂ मᱶ संशोधन 
ᳰकया है। 
(ii) सरकार ने नवंबर, 2021 मᱶ, भारतीय िशपयाडᭅ मᱶ िनᳶमᭅत ᳰकए जाने हेतु टगᲂ कᳱ खरीद क े  िलए 
महापᱫनᲂ ᳇ारा उपयोग हेतु पाँच ᮧकार के  मानक टग िडज़ाइन जारी ᳰकए हᱹ।  
(iii) ᭭वदेशी पोत िनमाᭅण को बढ़ावा देने क े िलए, मंᮢालय ने 20.09.2023 को ᳰकसी भी ᮧकार क े 
जलयान चाटᭅर, िजसे िनिवदा ᮧᳰᮓया क े  मा᭟यम से भारतीय िनᳶमᭅत, भारतीय ᭟वज वाले और 
भारतीय ᭭वािम᭜व वाले जलयानᲂ को ᮧाथिमकता देकर िलया जाता है, मᱶ पालन ᳰकए जाने वाले 
‘ᮧथम अ᭭वीकार करने का अिधकार (आरओएफआर)’ अनुᮓम को संशोिधत ᳰकया है,  
(iv) मंᮢालय ने 16 अग᭭त, 2024 को ᮕीन टग ᮝांिज़शन ᮧोᮕाम (जीटीटीपी) शुᱨ ᳰकया है, िजसका 
उ᳎े᭫य पयाᭅवरण कᳱ दृि᳥ से अनुक ू ल टगबोट संचालनᲂ को अपनाने को ᮧो᭜सािहत करके  काबᭅन 
उ᭜सजᭅन को कम करना और पयाᭅवरण पर पड़ने वाले ᮧभाव को कम से कम करना है।  
(v) सरकार ने अंतदᱷशीय जलयानᲂ क े िलए हᳯरत नौका ᳰदशािनदᱷश जारी ᳰकए हᱹ, िजनका उ᳎े᭫य 
अंतदᱷशीय जलमागᭅ जलयानᲂ मᱶ हᳯरत ᮧौ᳒ोिगᳰकयᲂ को अपनाने को बढ़ावा देना है। 
(vi) भारत सरकार ने 13 अᮧैल, 2016 कᳱ राजपᮢ अिधसूचना सं᭎या 112 क े  मा᭟यम से अ᳒तन 
हामᲃनाइ᭔ड मा᭭टर िल᭭ट ऑफ इंᮨा᭭ᮝ᭍चर सब-से᭍टसᭅ मᱶ 'िशपयाडᭅ' को शािमल ᳰकया है। 
(vii) ᭭वदेशी पोत िनमाᭅण को बढ़ावा देने क े  िलए, सरकार ने 19.05.2016 को सरकारी िवभागᲂ या 
एजᱶिसयᲂ, िजनमᱶ सावᭅजिनक ᭃेᮢ क े  उपᮓम भी शािमल हᱹ, ᳇ारा सरकारी उ᳎े᭫यᲂ या अपने ᭭वयं 
क े  ᮧयोग के िलए उपयोग ᳰकए जाने वाले ᳰकसी भी ᮧकार क े  जलयान क े  अिधᮕहण क े  िलए नए 
पोत िनमाᭅण क े  ᳰदए गए ऑडᭅरᲂ कᳱ िनिवदाᲐ क े  मू᭨यांकन और उ᭠हᱶ सᲅपने क े  ᳰदशािनदᱷश जारी 
ᳰकए हᱹ। जब भी ᳰकसी जलयाान का अिधᮕहण िनिवदा क े  मा᭟यम से ᳰकया जाता है, तो पाᮢ 
भारतीय िशपयाडᲄ को "ᮧथम अ᭭वीकार करने का अिधकार" ᮧा᳙ होगा ताᳰक वे िवदेशी िशपयाडᭅ 
᳇ारा ᮧ᭭तािवत ᭠यूनतम मू᭨य क े  बराबर मू᭨य का ᮧ᭭ताव दे सकᱶ। इस ᮧयास का उ᳎े᭫य भारतीय 
िशपयाडᲄ मᱶ पोत िनमाᭅण गितिविधयᲂ को बढ़ावा देना है। इसके अितᳯरᲦ, पोत िनमाᭅण और पोत-
᭭वािम᭜व से संबंिधत सरकारी सं᭭थानᲂ को भारत सरकार क े  सावᭅजिनक खरीद (मेक इन इंिडया 
को वरीयता) आदेश, 2017 के अनुसार ᭭थानीय सामᮕी सुिनि᳟त करने के िलए कहा गया है। इस 
आदेश क े  अनुसार, ₹200 करोड़ से कम मू᭨य क े जलयानᲂ कᳱ खरीद भारतीय िशपयाडᲄ से ही कᳱ 
जानी अपेिᭃत है। 
 
(घ): िपछले दशक मᱶ देश क े  तटीय नौवहन ᭃेᮢ मᱶ तीᮯ वृि᳍ देखी गई है, िजसमᱶ कागᲃ यातायात िवᱫ वषᭅ 
2014-15 के  86.3 िमिलयन टन (एमटी) से लगभग दोगुना बढ़कर िवᱫ वषᭅ 2024-25 मᱶ 165.4 मीᳯᮝक 
टन हो गया है। 
 
933                                                      

(ङ): आव᭫यक पᳯरसंपिᱫयᲂ के  समावेशन/आधुिनकᳱकरण, तटीय िनगरानी उ᳖यनᲂ, ᭃेᮢीय साझेदाᳯरयᲂ 
और एजᱶिसयᲂ क े बीच सूचना साझा करने कᳱ पहलᲂ क े  मा᭟यम से 'समुᮤी सुरᭃा' को बढ़ाया गया है। समुᮤी 
और तटीय सुरᭃा को सुदृढ़ करने के िलए, िन᳜िलिखत िविश᳥ उपाय ᳰकए गए हᱹ:- 
i)  भारतीय नौसेना को समᮕ समुᮤी सुरᭃा के  िलए उᱫरदायी ᮧािधकारी क े  ᱨप मᱶ नािमत ᳰकया 
गया है, िजसमᱶ तटीय सुरᭃा और अपतटीय सुरᭃा शािमल है। 
ii)  भारतीय तटरᭃक बल (आईसीजी) को तटीय पुिलस ᳇ारा ग᭫त ᳰकए जाने वाले ᭃेᮢ सिहत भू-
भागीय जल मᱶ तटीय सुरᭃा क े  िलए उᱫरदायी ᮧािधकारी क े  ᱨप मᱶ नािमत ᳰकया गया है। 
iii)  सभी िहतधारकᲂ ᳇ारा तटीय ᭃेᮢᲂ और ईईजेड मᱶ पोतᲂ और िवमानᲂ ᳇ारा ग᭫त/िनगरानी बढ़ाई 
गई है। 
iv)  आईसीजी, भारत क े समुᮤी ᭃेᮢᲂ मᱶ िनगरानी और सुरᭃा कायᲄ क े  िलए ᮧितᳰदन 18-20 पोत, 30-
35 नाव/यान और 10-12 िवमान तैनात करता है। 
v)  समुᮤ मᱶ मछली पकड़ने वाली नौकाᲐ और अ᭠य ᮧचालकᲂ क े  ᳞ िᲦगत ᭣यौरᲂ कᳱ ᮧमािणकता कᳱ 
जाँच के  िलए िनयिमत ᱨप से बोᳺडᲈग ऑपरेशन। 
vi)  सभी िहतधारकᲂ क े  बीच सम᭠वय क े  िलए सभी तटीय रा᭔यᲂ/संघ रा᭔य ᭃेᮢᲂ मᱶ तटीय सुरᭃा क े 
िलए मानक संचालन ᮧᳰᮓयाएँ (एसओपी) ᮧकािशत कᳱ गई हᱹ। 
vii) मानक संचालन ᮧᳰᮓयाᲐ और तटीय सुरᭃा तंᮢ कᳱ पुि᳥ करने क े  िलए िनयिमत ᱨप से तटीय 
सुरᭃा अ᭤यास और तटीय सुरᭃा ᮧचालन कायᭅ करना। 
viii) 46 रडार ᭭टेशनᲂ वाली तट आधाᳯरत ि᭭थर सᱶसर चेन (सीएसएस) क े मा᭟यम से इले᭍ᮝॉिनक 
िनगरानी रखी जाती है। इसके अितᳯरᲦ, सीएसएस पᳯरयोजना के दूसरे चरण मᱶ 38 रडार ᭭टेशन 
᭭थािपत ᳰकए जा रहे हᱹ। 
ix) आईसीजी, समुᮤी और तटीय सुरᭃा को मजबूत करने क े  िलए जागᱨकता बढ़ाने हेतु मछुआरᲂ क े 
िलए िनयिमत सामुदाियक संपकᭅ कायᭅᮓम (सीआईपी) आयोिजत कर रहा है। सीआईपी के दौरान, 
मछुआरᲂ को इस दृि᳥ से सुरᭃा एजᱶिसयᲂ को सतकᭅ करने कᳱ आव᭫यकता क े  बारे मᱶ भी अवगत 
कराया जाता है ᳰक जब भी वे समुᮤ मᱶ कोई भी संᳰद᭏ध/िवदेशी नाव देखे तो वे उस बारे मᱶ बताएं।

1915 ᮰ी आर. िगᳯरराजन :

᭭थािपत करने कᳱ पहल कᳱ है, त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या है; 
(ख) तिमलनाडु के तीन ᮧमुख पᱫनᲂ मᱶ से ᮧ᭜येक से क ु ल ᳰकतनी आय अᳶजत ᱟई है, िपछले पांच वषᲄ मᱶ 
पᱫनᲂ क े  िव᭭तार और िवकास क े  िलए पᱫन-वार ᳰकतनी धनरािश उपल᭣ध कराई गई है; और 
(ग) ᭍या चे᳖ई कामराज पᱫन और क ु᲻ालोर सागरमाला पᳯरयोजना के  अंतगᭅत हᱹ, त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या 
है? 
 
उᱫर

हाँ, तो त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या है और यᳰद नहᱭ, तो इसक े  ᭍या कारण हᱹ; 
(ख) ᭍या जल वाहक योजना मᱶ इलेि᭍ᮝक, हाइिᮩड या एलएनजी चािलत जैसे हᳯरत जहाज़ᲂ को अपनाने क े 
िलए कोई अिनवायᭅता या ᮧो᭜साहन ᳰदया गया है; 
(ग) ᭍या जल वाहक योजना क े  कायाᭅ᭠वयन क े कारण कागᲃ टन भार मᱶ ᮧ᭜यᭃ वृि᳍ कᳱ िनगरानी करने क े 
िलए कोई कायᭅ-िन᭬पादन मू᭨यांकन ᮧणाली ᭭थािपत कᳱ गई है; और 
(घ) यᳰद हाँ, तो त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या है? 
  
उᱫर 
पᱫन, पोत पᳯरवहन और जलमागᭅ मंᮢी  
(᮰ी सबाᭅनंद सोणोवाल) 
  
(क): भारतीय नौवहन िनगम (एससीआई) कᳱ पूणᭅ ᭭वािम᭜व वाली सहायक क ं पनी, अंतदᱷशीय एवं तटीय 
नौवहन िलिमटेड (आईसीएसएल), जल वाहक योजना कᳱ कायाᭅ᭠वयन एजᱶसी है। जल वाहक योजना के 
अंतगᭅत, जलमागᭅ याᮢा पर ᳰकए गए क ु ल वा᭭तिवक ᮧचालन ᳞ य क े  35% तक क े िवᱫीय ᮧो᭜साहन का 
ᮧावधान है। योजना क े अनुसार, आईसीएसएल को िवᱫीय वषᭅ के अंत मᱶ एक ᳯरपोटᭅ क े  साथ उपयोग कᳱ 
गई रािश का सांिविधक लेखा परीᭃक ᳇ारा िविधवत ᮧमािणत उपयोग ᮧमाण-पᮢ ᮧ᭭तुत करना अपेिᭃत 
है।  
 
(ख): योजना का उ᳎े᭫य (i) कागᲃ क े  मॉडल को अंतदᱷशीय जल पᳯरवहन (आईड᭣᭨यूटी) मोड मᱶ िश᭢ट करने 
को ᮧो᭜साहन देकर ऐसे िश᭢ट को ᮧो᭜सािहत करना और (ii) िहतधारकᲂ का िव᳡ास बढ़ाने क े  उ᳎े᭫य से 
आईड᭣᭨यूटी ᭃेᮢ कᳱ िव᳡सनीयता और त᭜परता ᮧदᳶशᭅत करना है।   
 
(ग) और (घ): जल वाहक योजना क े  िन᭬पादन मू᭨यांकन क े  िलए प᭜ तन, पोत परिवहन और जलमागᭅ

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO.- 151 
ANSWERED ON- 04/08/2025 
 
IRREGULARITIES IN LPG DISTRIBUTION AND SUBSIDY TRANSFER 
 
*151 SHRI IMRAN PRATAPGARHI: 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware of widespread irregularities in LPG distribution, including 
delays in Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) of subsidies and the presence of ghost beneficiaries, 
particularly in rural areas; 
 
(b) the total number of such cases reported during the last three years and action taken thereon; 
 
(c) whether Government will initiate a nationwide social audit of LPG subsidy transfers to 
identify systemic lapses; and 
 
(d) whether it plans to strengthen the grievance redressal mechanism to ensure timely resolution 
and accountability in subsidy disbursements? 
ANSWER 
 
 MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS 
 (SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI) 
 
(a) to (d):   A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
945                                                      

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (d) IN RESPECT OF THE 
RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 151 FOR REPLY ON 04.08.2025 
REGARDING ‘IRREGULARITIES IN LPG DISTRIBUTION AND SUBSIDY 
TRANSFER’ ASKED BY SHRI IMRAN PRATAPGARHI. 
 
(a): Government continues to take measures on ongoing basis to ensure that LPG distribution and 
subsidy transfers in respect of domestic LPG consumers are efficient, transparent, and inclusive. 
Implementation of initiatives like the PAHAL (DBTL) scheme, Aadhaar-based verification, 
biometric authentication and weeding out of ineligible or duplicate connections have significantly 
strengthened the system of transfers of targeted subsidies. 
Transformation of LPG distribution system 
Strengthening Beneficiary Targeting under PMUY- 
As of July 1, 2025 the total number of active domestic LPG consumers in India stands at 33.05 
crore, which includes 10.33 crore beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY). 
This represents a significant increase from 14.51 crore domestic LPG consumers as of April 1, 
2014, reflecting the Government’s successful efforts to expand access to clean cooking fuel.  
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May, 2016 with an objective to provide 
deposit free LPG connection to adult women from poor households across the country. The 
primary objective of PMUY is to provide LPG connections to poor households, in order to protect 
their health from the adverse effects of traditional cooking fuels such as firewood, coal, and cow 
dung, which are known to cause serious indoor air pollution and related health hazards. 
Implementation of PMUY has contributed to improvement in LPG coverage in the country from 
62% in April 2016 to near saturation now. 
Expanding Rural LPG Access- 
In order to improve access of LPG in rural and remote areas, out of 7997 distributorships 
commissioned during 01.04.2016 to 30.06.2025 across the country, 7403 (i.e. 93 %) are 
catering to rural areas. As of July 01, 2025, there are a total of 25,573 LPG distributorships across 
the country, out of which 17,646 are serving rural areas.  
 
946                                                      

Delivery Monitoring and Consumer Empowerment- 
To enhance consumer empowerment and improve service transparency, IVRS/SMS refill booking 
system has been implemented across the Country in all LPG distributorships. Under this system, 
consumers receive SMS notifications at key stages — refill booking, cash memo generation, and 
refill delivery —which allows them to track their transactions and report any cases of wrong or 
non-delivery. In addition, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have introduced the Delivery 
Authentication Code (DAC). This code is sent to the consumer via SMS upon cash memo 
generation and is required to be shared with the delivery personnel at the time of delivery, thereby 
ensuring delivery authentication. 
Field Inspections and Checks-  
To ensure compliance and curb malpractices, both Regular and Surprise Inspections of LPG 
distributors are done by Field Officers of the OMCs. Also, officers from Regional Offices/ Zonal 
Offices/ Divisional Offices/ Territory Offices and officials from Anti Adulteration Cell/ Quality 
Reassurance Cells and Vigilance Department conduct random checks at Distributors’ Godown/ 
Showroom/delivery points, as well as en-route to ensure that no misuse of LPG takes place. 
Reforms in Subsidy Transfers and Strengthening of the system 
Direct Benefit Transfer of LPG (DBTL)-PAHAL Scheme has been implemented since January 
2015 for transparent and effective disbursal of subsidy across the country. Under PAHAL 
Scheme, all domestic LPG cylinders are sold at non-subsidised price and applicable subsidy to 
LPG consumers is transferred directly into the bank account of the consumers.  
Once the subsidy is credited, the consumer receives an SMS on their registered mobile number 
confirming the subsidy deposit. In the event of a failed transaction, the consumer is informed of 
the issue along with the necessary corrective action to be taken through SMS.  
PAHAL has played a crucial role in identification and blocking of ‘ghost’ accounts, multiple 
accounts, and inactive LPG connections, thereby helping curb the diversion of subsidised LPG for 
commercial use. As of 01.07.2025, 4.08 crore duplicate, fake/non-existent, and inactive LPG 
connections are blocked/suspended/deactivated. 
 
947                                                      

Government has taken numerous steps to remove ineligible consumers and improve subsidy 
transfer process, which include the following: 
De-duplication through CLDP- 
Government has also brought a Common LPG Database Platform (CLDP) through which 
duplicate connections are being identified and removed from the LPG database. Deduplication 
amongst LPG consumer database is done using Aadhaar Number, Bank Account Details, AHL 
TIN Number, Ration Card Details, Name and Address as the key parameters. 
Biometric Aadhaar Authentication Drive- 
Aadhaar-based authentication for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) schemes enables accurate, real-
time, and cost-effective identification, authentication, and de-duplication of beneficiaries, 
ensuring targeted delivery of benefits to the intended recipients. To strengthen consumer 
authentication, the Government had directed the public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) 
to undertake and complete biometric Aadhaar authentication of PMUY and PAHAL beneficiaries. 
As of 01.07.2025, Biometric Aadhaar authentication has been completed for 67% of the existing 
PMUY beneficiaries. Further, all new PMUY consumers undergo Biometric Authentication 
before release of connections. 
Weeding out of Ineligible Consumers- 
PAHAL has enabled the disbursement of the Targeted subsidy benefit to PMUY consumers. 
Multiple steps have been taken to ensure that these benefits reach the eligible and targeted 
beneficiaries in an efficient and timely manner. Since its inception, as a result of comprehensive 
deduplication exercises undertaken, a total of 8.49 lakh PMUY connections have been terminated. 
Further, in January 2025, a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) was issued for the removal of 
PMUY consumers who had not taken any further refills after the installation of their connection. 
Under this SOP, around 12,000 inactive PMUY connections have already been terminated. 
Reducing Transaction Failures by Enhancing Aadhaar Compliance- 
While most subsidy transactions are completed successfully within 2 days of delivery, some 
issues have been observed leading to transaction failure during DBTL subsidy transfer such as 
deseeding of consumer Aadhaar from bank account, merger of banks, Inactive Aadhaar number,

(a) to (d) The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) conducts
investigations of accidents & serious incidents in accordance with the Aircraft
(Investigation of Accidents & Incidents) Rules, 2017 and the Standards &
Recommended Practices of International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO)
Annex 13. All investigations under these Rules are conducted in a fair, impartial
and judicious manner, adhering to the relevant standards of Annex 13.
 
A preliminary report on the accident was published by the AAIB on 12.07.2025
and is available on their website at www.aaib.gov.in. The report is based on the
factual information available at the time and does not include any conclusions.
 
The investigation is ongoing and will examine all the aspects to determine the
probable cause(s)/ contributory factor(s) leading to the accident. The sole objective
of the investigation of an accident or incident shall be the prevention of accidents
and incidents and not to apportion blame or liability.
 
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has established comprehensive
Civil Aviation Regulations to ensure the safe operation and maintenance of
aircraft. These regulations are continuously updated and aligned with international
standards, including those of ICAO and European Union Aviation Safety Agency
(EASA). DGCA amends its regulations from time to time in accordance with
ICAO standards.
 
Under these regulations, operators are required to comply with guidelines issued
by manufacturers, such as Service Bulletins, Airworthiness Directives (ADs), and
Maintenance Planning Documents (MPDs).
 
To ensure effective safety oversight, the DGCA has implemented a structured
surveillance and audit framework.

(a) and (b)  Since August 2019, Government of India in partnership with States/UTs is 
implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of potable water to 
every rural household of the country, through functional tap water connection. 
 
Drinking Water being a State subject, the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation, and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes/ works, 
including those under the Jal Jeevan Mission, lies with State/UT Governments. The 
Government of India supports the States by providing technical and financial assistance.   
 
Thus, details of individual projects/schemes which inter -alia include collapse or bursting of 
newly constructed water tanks during testing or soon after commissioning of rural water 
supply projects are maintained at the State Government level. According to  the information 
provided by the State/UTs, such incidents have not occurred in any state other than four states 
namely Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan. The said states have informed 
that some incidents have occurred in rural areas in the last two years and the current year. The 
State-wise, year-wise along with district-wise details are given below: 
 
State Year District 
Uttar Pradesh 2023 Balrampur 
Uttar Pradesh 2024 Sitapur 
Uttar Pradesh 2025 Kanpur Nagar 
Uttar Pradesh 2025 Lakhimpur Kheri 
Uttar Pradesh 2025 Sitapur 
Jharkhand 2024 Palamu 
Jharkhand 2024 Koderma 
Madhya Pradesh 2024 Rewa 
Rajasthan  2025 Churu 
 
(c) to (e)  To ensure the quality of the work under the operational guideline for the 
implementation of the JJM, third party inspection and certification before payment is 
mandatory. For the purpose, States/UTs have been empowered to empanel third party 
inspection agencies (TPIA) to check the quality of work executed by the agencies, quality of 
materials used for construction and quality of machinery installed in each of the scheme.  
 
The criteria for selection and Terms of References (ToR) of TPIAs to be empanelled by the 
States/UTs is laid down in JJM Guidelines. The details of quality checks done by TPIAs are 
maintained at State Level. The supply of the material to be used in the scheme is done after 
inspection through factory visit conducted by these agencies. Other building and steel related 
materials are also inspected before its use.  
 
Provisions have been made to use such materials only after supply meeting the standards. The 
grievances/ complaints regarding implementation of JJM in States including inferior qual ity 
of work, as and when received in Ministry of Jal Shakti are forwarded to States for taking 
corrective measures.  
 
954                                                      

Page 3 of 3 
 
It is stated that State of Uttar Pradesh , Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh  and Rajasthan  have 
informed that a detailed technical enquiry has been conducted by the technical team  in each 
case of collapsing of water tanks.  
 
Uttar Pradesh Government has informed that in four cases, quality of Zinc Alume Sheets, nut 
and bolts got tested from IIT Kanp ur, were found in general satisfactory except some 
parameters in case of Balrampur . The main reasons for collapsing of water tanks  were 
improper fusing of zinc alume sheets, improper jointing of these sheets at outlet and washout 
pipe locations , non-compliance of the prescribed water filling protocol during the hydro 
testing of the tank , substandard construction material (Concrete) used in staging work and 
structural failure.  
 
State of Uttar Pradesh has taken actions as imposition of penalty along with removal of the 
concerned engineers of  the construction agency and third -party agenc y & action against 
officials including Executive  Engineers and Assistant Engineers of Jal  Nigam. All the 
contractors have been directed to reconstruct the OHT at their own cost. 
 
Similarly, State of Jharkhand has informed that the main reason for collapsing of water tanks 
was poor workmanship. And action for blacklisting of the agency & rescinding of work have 
been taken.  Further, action has been taken against the officials including the Executive 
Engineers. 
 
Further, State of Madhya Pradesh has informed that the main reasons for collapsing of water 
tank in Rewa is loose compacted compressible cohesive clayey soil and non -availability of 
RAAFT Foundation for reducing the structure failure. However, State has taken action against 
the officials. Also, the contractor has proposed to construct the tank for which no addi tional 
payment will be made by the State Government. 
 
State of Rajasthan has informed that the reason for the collapse of water tank is failure of 
columns in compression /buckling. In this regard, enquiry committee has recommended that 
case may be referred to a reputed institute to examine correctness of approved design/drawing 
to assess the quality of the executed work and to determine the actual cause of collapse of this 
OHSR. Further action against concerned official has been initiated by the State.

(a)   Government of India is committed to make provision for safe & potable tap water supply in 
adequate quantity, of prescribed quality and on a regular & long -term basis to all rural 
households in the country. Towards this end, in August 2019, Government of India is 
implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) in partnership with States to make provision of tap water 
supply to every rural household. 
  
At the time of launch of JJM, out of total 19. 36 Crore rural households, 3.23 Crore rural 
households (16.71%) of the country had tap water connections. Since then, about 12. 44 Crore 
families living in rural areas have been provided with tap water connections in their homes and 
as on 30.07.2025, about 15.68 Crore (80.97%) households are having tap water connections. 
 
Water being a state subject, the responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation, 
and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes/ works, including those under the Jal Jeevan 
Mission, lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the States by 
providing technical and financial assistance. 
 
As reported by State Govt. of Karnataka, in Belgaum District, at the start of Jal Jeevan Mission 
in August 2019, only 1,92,063  (22.53%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connection. Since then, around 5,72,418 additional rural households have been reported to have 
been provided with tap water connection  and as on 30.07.2025,  out of total 8,52,433  rural 
households, about 7,64,481 (89.68%) rural households are having tap water connections  in the 
district. 
 
(b) As reported by Govt. of Karnataka, the details of multi -village schemes (MVS) in Belgaum 
district is as follows: - 
 
Total no. of MVS Completed Ongoing Work order not issued 
1165 328 824 13 
 
(c) Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, as per existing guidelines, Bureau of Indian Standards’ 
BIS:10500 standards are adopted as benchmark for quality of water being supplied through the 
piped water supply schemes. BIS specifies ‘acceptable limit’ and ‘permissible limit in the 
absence of alternate source’ for various phy sio-chemical and bacteriological parameters for 
drinking water quality. 
 
Under JJM, while planning water supply schemes to provide tap water supply to households, 
priority is given to habitations affected by chemical contaminants.  States/ UTs have been 
advised to plan and implement piped water supply schemes based on alternative safe water 
sources for the villages with water quality issues.  
 
Under JJM, States/ UTs have been advised to install Community Water Purification Plants 
(CWPPs) especially in Arsen ic and Fluoride affected habitations to provide potable water to 
every household to meet their drinking and cooking requirements till the commissioning of piped 
water supply schemes compliant to JJM standards. As reported by States/ UTs on JJM -IMIS as 
on date, there are 314 Arsenic and 248 Fluoride affected rural habitations in the country where 
the piped water supply schemes compliant to JJM standards are yet to be commissioned. 
However, all these habitations (314 for Arsenic and 248 for Fluoride) have bee n provided with 
safe drinking water through CWPPs/ IHPs. Thus, all habitations in rural area of the country are 
provided safe drinking water free from Arsenic and Fluoride contamination. 
 
957                                                      

Page 3 of 3 
 
In consultation with various stakeholders 'Concise Handbook for Moni toring Water Quality of 
Piped Drinking Water Supply to Rural Households’ has been released in December 2024 for 
guidance to States/ UT’s officials and their parastatal organizations. The handbook 
recommended for a comprehensive testing of drinking water sa mples at various testing points 
such as source, treatment plant, storage and distribution points, and remedial action wherever 
necessary, to ensure that the water supplied to households is of prescribed quality. The 
recommended remedial action includes the immediate closure of chemically contaminated water 
sources, notifying the result to the relevant authorities and affected communities, providing safe 
drinking water as per JJM guidelines (at least 8-10 lpcd) through a safe source or through tankers 
immediately within 24 hrs till piped water supply is restored, implementing emergency treatment 
measures such as cleaning of OHTs, check pipe line leakage, etc. within 7 days, testing all basic 
and area-specific chemical as well as bacteriological parameters, and, if found safe, restore water 
supply from a safe source in case of chemical contaminants.  On the other hand, in case of 
bacterial contamination, immediate action (within 24 hrs) must be taken, which includes proper 
disinfection, intimate concern for aut hority and affected communities, and temporary 
arrangements to provide safe drinking water through tankers (8 -10 LPCD).

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (D) IN RESPECT OF 
RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 155 FOR REPLY ON 04.08.2025 
REGARDING EXPANSION OF CITY GAS DISTRIBUTION NETWORK AND 
CONSUMER BALANCE ASKED BY SHRI TEJVEER SINGH 
(a) to (c) Government have taken multiple steps to increase share of Natural Gas in primary 
energy mix. This includes expansion of National Gas Grid Pipeline, expansion of City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) network, setting up of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Terminals, allocation 
of domestic gas to Compressed Natural Gas (Transport) / Piped Natural Gas (Domestic) 
CNG(T)/PNG(D) as priority sector, allowing marketing and pricing freedom with a ceiling 
price to gas produced from high pressure/high temperature areas, deep water & ultra-deep 
water and from coal seams, Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation 
(SATAT) initiatives to promote CBG etc.  
Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed 
Natural Gas (CNG) stations are part of development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Networks. 
The same is carried out by the entities authorized by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory 
Board (PNGRB) as per their Minimum Work Programme (MWP). PNGRB has authorized 
entities for development of CGD network in 307 Geographical Areas (GAs), covering the 
entire mainland area for the development of CGD network across the country. 
The expansion of CGD network is a continuous process. During the year 2024–25, 57 
new districts have been connected across various States under the CGD network, the details of 
which are at Annexure –I.  
 Government does not prescribe the selling price of PNG. The retail price of PNG in any 
GA is determined by the CGD entity after considering basic cost of gas, supply and distribution 
cost, entity margin and state taxes/ VAT. However, with a view to ensuring transparency and 
disclosure, the Government have issued guidelines to all CGD entities to furnish the complete 
breakup of PNG (Domestic) price on the invoice raised to the consumer. The breakup is to 
include the cost of gas to the entity, supply and distribution cost, entity’s margin, VAT and any 
other tax. PNGRB also requires every authorized entity to incorporate in the consumer bill or 
invoice key information including consumption details, charges for last mile connectivity, 
taxes, levies, and sale price of gas supplied.  
To address the grievances of individual consumers, Section 25 of the PNGRB Act, 
2006 states that the complaints of the individual consumers are maintainable before the 
consumer disputes redressal forum under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Further, to 
protect the interest of the consumers, Regulation 11 of the PNGRB (Code of Practice for 
Quality of Service for City or Local Natural Gas Distribution Networks) Regulations, 2010 
specifies creation of a Consumer Complaint Cell by the authorized CGD entity for registration 
of complaints/grievances personally, over telephone or through e-mail. Emergency contact 
numbers and Customer Care numbers of all CGD entities hosted on the PNGRB website are at 
Annexure-II. Further, the consumers can also lodge their grievances to the public authorities 
on any subject related to service delivery on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and 
Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) portal. 
960                                                      

(d) As outlined above, the Government have taken various initiatives to enhance the reach of 
CGD network across the country. These initiatives have led to provisioning of more than 1.50 
Crore PNG Domestic (PNG (D)) connections, establishing of more than 8000 CNG stations 
and laying of over 5.9 lakh inch-km pipeline. 
The spread of Natural Gas (including rural and tribal areas) is also facilitated by the 
development of National Gas Grid. Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is 
the authority to grant authorization to entities to lay, build, operate and expand Natural Gas 
Pipelines (NGPL).  PNGRB has authorized approximately 34200 km of NGPL network which 
include common carrier, spur line, tie-in connectivity and dedicated pipeline across the country 
to various entities out of which 25429 km have been made operational as on 31.03.2025. Upon 
completion of balance pipeline, which is under construction, the National Gas Grid will 
connect all major demand centres. This would ensure availability of Natural Gas across all 
regions (including rural and tribal areas) and facilitate downstream development of CGD 
networks, and also potentially help to achieve uniform economic and social progress. 
The Government with the endeavor to provide cleaner cooking fuel have also been 
promoting LPG as a cooking fuel. As of July 01, 2025, there are a total of 33.05 Crore LPG 
connections. Further, with an objective to provide deposit free LPG connection to adult women 
from poor households across the country, Pradhan Mantri UjjwalaYojana (PMUY) was 
launched in May, 2016. As on 01.07.2025, there are 10.33 Crore PMUY connections across the 
country. More than 80% of PMUY connections are serving rural areas. About 3.13 Crore LPG 
connections have been released to SC/ST or households. Further, to enhance access of LPG in 
rural areas, 17646 distributors are serving rural areas out of a total of 25573 distributors in the 
country.  
With the objective of promoting rural economy, the Government have been laying 
emphasis on setting up Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plants in the rural areas under the 
Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) scheme using 
agricultural waste, animal waste, press mud, etc. as feedstock (mainly found in rural and tribal 
areas). This facilitates localized Compressed Bio Gas generation and supports rural 
employment and entrepreneurship. As on July 01, 2025, a total of 113 CBG plants have been 
commissioned with a total production capacity of 775 TPD (out of which 95 plants utilize 
agricultural waste, animal waste, press mud).

of organization /aircraft, which includes regular and periodic audits, spot checks,
night surveillance and ramp inspections across all operators, including continuous
oversight of maintenance practices. In case there is a violation, DGCA takes
enforcement action as per its Enforcement Policy and Procedure Manual.
 
Post-accident of Air India flight AI-171 Boeing 787 aircraft on 12.06.2025, DGCA
has ordered to conduct the checks/inspections of all 33 787-Dreamliner aircraft of
Air India.
 
Out of total 33 aircraft, 31 operational aircraft have been inspected wherein minor
findings were observed in 8 aircraft. These aircraft have been released for
operation post rectification. The remaining 2 aircraft are under scheduled
maintenance.

revenues on such routes.

transport and similar facilities in 32 cities of the State of Madhya Pradesh under the  AMRUT 
Scheme; 
(b) the number of urban local bodies where work is in progress under AMRUT 2.0; and 
(c) the sectors in which the State attained key achievements under the AMRUT Scheme? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANOHAR LAL)

986                                                      

 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 160 REGARDING “ WORK UNDERTAKEN IN MADHYA PRADESH UNDER 
AMRUT & AMRUT 2.0 SCHEME”, DUE FOR ANSWER IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 04th 
AUGUST, 2025.  
 
(a): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) is implementing Atal Mission for 
Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), which was launched on 25 June 2015 in 
selected 500 cities (485 cities including 15 merged cities) and towns across the country including 
34 cities in Madhya Pradesh. The Mission focuses on development of basic infrastructure, in the 
selected cities and towns, in the sectors of water supply, sewerage and septage management, etc. 
 
Under AMRUT, State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) amounting to ₹6,200.67 crore 
including committed Central Assistance of ₹2,592.86 crore have been approved for projects in 
Madhya Pradesh State for the entire Mission period. As reported by the State on AMRUT portal, 
216 projects worth ₹6,765.91 crore have been taken up by the State. Project have been taken up in 
the key sectors including 32 Water Supply projects worth ₹2,280.8 crore, 29 S ewerage/septage 
management projects worth ₹3,880.56 crore, 23 Drainage projects worth ₹248.32 crore, etc. 
 
(b): AMRUT 2.0 scheme has been launched on 01 October, 2021 in all Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs)/ cities. Under AMRUT 2.0, States/UTs are empowered to select, prioritise, design, implement 
and monitor the projects within the broad framework of Mission guidelines. So far, under AMRUT 
2.0 a total of 1,273 projects worth ₹12,963.14 crore (including Operations & Maintenance cost) in 418 
Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ cities  of Madhya Pradesh have been approved by MoHUA which 
includes 417 Water supply projects worth ₹6,889.58 crore, 36 sewerage/septage management projects 
worth ₹5,432.04 crore, 430 water body rejuvenation projects worth ₹511.75 crore and 390 green 
spaces and park projects worth ₹129.77 crore. As reported by the State  on AMRUT 2.0 portal, there 
are 999 projects worth ₹6,597.20 crore in 411 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ cities  in which contracts 
have been awarded/ completed.  
 
(c):  As reported by the State, under AMRUT Mission and in convergence with other schemes of 
the State, 14.41 lakh water tap connections (new/ serviced) and 4.02 lakh sewer connections (new/ 
serviced) (including households covered through Faecal Sludge and Septage Management -FSSM) 
have been provided in the State of Madhya Pradesh. 613.85 Million Litre Per Day (MLD) Sewerage 
Treatment Capacity (STP) and 334.5 MLD Water Treatment Capacity (WTP) have been developed; 
188.12 kilometers length of drains have been constructed and; 422.06 acres of green space have 
been developed.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 
*161 TO BE ANSWERED ON 04.08.2025 IN RAJYA SABHA RE GARDING “RELEASE OF 
WATERS BY DVC TO THE STATE OF WEST BENGAL”  
(a)     Yes. Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) has relea sed 27,987 lakh cubic meters of water from 
Maithon and Panchet Reservoirs from 18 
th  June 2025 to 15 th  July 2025. 
  
(b) to (d)       Decisions regarding releases from the Maithon and P anchet Reservoirs of the DVC are made 
by the Damodar Valley Reservoir Regulation Committe e (DVRRC). This committee is chaired by the 
Member (River Management), Central Water Commission  (CWC), New Delhi, and includes 
representatives from the CWC, DVC, Government of West Bengal and Government of Jharkhand. 
DVRRC has been mandated to guide DVC in release of water from the Maithon and Panchet 
reservoirs in a co-ordinated manner with due regard to ensure effective flood control as well as to fulfill the 
requirements of drinking, irrigation, navigation an d industrial uses for optimal benefits of State of West 
Bengal, State of Jharkhand and DVC. DVRRC follows a  very systematic and scientific approach for 
reservoir operation as per laid down procedure in D amodar Valley Reservoir Regulation Manual approved 
for the management of DVC reservoirs, in consultati on with DVC, Govt. of West Bengal and Govt. of 
Jharkhand.

(b) the immediate and long-term measures taken so f ar under Atal Bhujal Yojana and Jal Shakti Abhiyan 
to stop this declining trend and ensure sustainable availability of potable water in urban areas?

 (SHRI C R PAATIL)

994                                                      

2 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (b) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 
*164 TO BE ANSWERED ON 04.08.2025 IN RAJYA SABHA RE GARDING “DECLINE IN 
GROUNDWATER LEVELS AND WATER MANAGEMENT MEASURES”  
(a)    Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) monitors groundwater levels throughout the country including 
the State of Jharkhand, four times in every year. The district-wise groundwater level data measured during 
Post monsoon (November), 2024 for the State of Jhar khand is given in Annexure-I. Perusal of data 
indicates that approximately 99% of the analysed we lls have depth to water level in the range of 0-10 
meters below ground level (mbgl). 
  Further, in order to assess the long-term fluctua tion in groundwater levels, district-wise groundwat er 
level data of November, 2024 for the State of Jharkhand has been compared with the decadal mean of data 
for the November month from 2014 to 2023. Such anal ysis indicates that about 60% of the monitored 
wells have registered rise in groundwater levels. District-wise details are provided in Annexure II.  
  
(b)    Water being a State subject, sustainable develop ment and management of groundwater resources is 
primarily the responsibility of the State Governmen ts. However, the Central Government facilitates the  
efforts of the State Governments by way of technica l and financial assistance through its various sche mes 
and projects. 
   In this direction, efforts of the Central Govern ment for augmenting the ground water resources of the 
country, including Jharkhand are mainly channeled t hrough the flagship campaign of Jal Shakti Abhiyan 
(JSA). JSA is a time bound and mission mode program me being conducted annually since 2019 by the 
M/o Jal Shakti, wherein all the efforts and funds u nder various schemes and projects are converged to 
deliver water harvesting and  artificial  recharge works on the ground. 
  Currently, JSA 2025 is underway in the country wi th special focus on over-exploited and critical 
areas. As per the available information, under JSA,  completion of around 5 lakh water conservation and  
artificial recharge works has been coordinated through convergence in Jharkhand in the last 4 years. 
  To further strengthen the momentum of Jal Shakti Abhiyan, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB): A 
Community-Driven Path to Water Sustainability in In dia has been launched by the Hon’ble Prime 
Minister with a vision to make rain water harvestin g a mass movement in the country. By promoting 
community ownership and responsibility, the initiat ive seeks to develop cost-eﬀective, local solutions  
tailored to speciﬁc water challenges across diﬀeren t regions. In Jharkhand, around 2798 such locally 
suited rainwater harvesting and ground water rechar ge structures have been built through convergence 
under phase 1.0 of JSJB. 
  Atal Bhujal Yojana, which is a pilot scale progra mme focusing on selected priority water stressed 
districts, is not being implemented in Jharkhand. 
995                                                      

3 
 
  With regard to sustainable availability of potabl e water in urban areas of Jharkhand, it is to state  that 
responsibility of the same lies mainly on the state  governments and urban local bodies. However, M/o 
Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), GoI, has been im plementing AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 Schemes, 
which are major initiatives to improve the quality of life in cities, including expanding water supply  
schemes and providing potable tap water connections.  
  As informed by the state, under AMRUT Mission and  through convergence, so far 2.99 lakh urban 
households have been provided water tap connections  (new/ serviced) against the target of 3.61 lakh, i n 
Jharkhand. To further expand the coverage of urban infrastructure, including water supply, AMRUT 2.0 is 
being implemented since 2021 in all statutory towns  of the country, to enable them to become 'self-rel iant' 
and 'water secure'. So far, under AMRUT 2.0, totall y 17 water supply projects and 70 water body 
rejuvenation projects have been approved by MoHUA for Jharkhand. 
  Furthermore, under Shallow Aquifer Management (SA M) of MoHUA, priority cities have been 
selected for addressing groundwater depletion and w ater logging, by taking up over 35 pilot recharge 
structures in 6 cities in various parts of the coun try, notably raising water levels by 2-3 feet. In J harkhand 
state, the city of Dhanbad is covered under this programme. 
  Thus, all the above schemes and programmes are wo rking in a synergic fashion for conservation, 
recharge and enhancing sustainability of water sour ces with an objective to ensure water and drinking 
water security of urban areas of the country, including in Jharkhand.

*165. DR. JOHN BRITTAS
999                                                      

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (C) IN RESPECT
OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.165 FOR REPLY ON
04.08.2025 REGARDING "DISPARITY IN INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR
DOMESTIC AND INTERNATIONAL FLIGHTS" ASKED BY DR. JOHN
BRITTAS.
 
(a) to (c): Insurance coverage for domestic flights are governed by limits of
liability under the 'Carriage by Air Act, 1972', while those for international flights
are regulated by ICAO under the Montreal Convention, 1999 to which India is a
signatory. The international obligations from the Montreal Convention have been
incorporated as separate provisions within the 'Carriage by Air Act, 1972'.
 
This Act provides for limits of liability for compensation to be provided to a
passenger in events such as death or bodily injury, delays in carriage, and the
destruction, loss, damage, or delay of baggage.The airlines maintain insurance for
an amount to adequately cover its liability to meet requisite compensation for
domestic and international flights. The maximum payouts, benefit types and policy
conditions are determined by the arrangement between the airline and the insurer.
 
Requirement for maintaining adequate insurance coverage towards liability for
compensation are ensured through extant Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR)
issued by DGCA while granting of Air Operator Certificate/Permit to Indian
carriers.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO : 1601
(TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4th August 2025)
 
DIRECT INTERNATIONAL FLIGHTS FROM CHANDIGARH AND
AMRITSAR AIRPORTS
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-
 
 
(a) whether Government is working on proposals or requests to initiate/increase the
number of direct international flights from Chandigarh and Amritsar airports to the
United Kingdom, Canada, and Singapore;
 
(b) if so, the current status of such proposals and timeline fixed for
implementation;
 
(c) the details of existing international routes operational from these airports; and
 
(d) whether any bilateral air service negotiations are underway to enhance
international connectivity from the State of Punjab to major global destinations
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
 
 
(a) to (d): International flight operations are governed by Bilateral Air Services
Agreement (ASA) between India and the respective countries. In accordance with
respective ASAs, Indian designated carriers are free to mount operations to/from
any international airport, including Chandigarh and Amritsar, to any foreign
destinations as per mutually agreed capacity limits. The start of direct international
flights from any point in India is purely a commercial decision of scheduled
airlines on the basis of passenger demand, availability of slots, economic viability
of the route, and other associated factors. The Government provides an enabling
environment for the growth of the civil aviation sector, but does not interfere in the
operational plans of the airlines.
 
Enhancing air capacity entitlements is a continuous process and is done through
bilateral agreements on air services signed between India and foreign countries
1601. SHRI SATNAM SINGH SANDHU
1001                                                      

from time to time, depending upon factors which include benefits to the Indian
aviation sector, presence of Indian diaspora in that country, future plans of Indian
carriers, elements of reciprocity, balance of benefits and other relevant factors
between two countries.
 
Presently, Amritsar Airport has international services to and from Birmingham,
Bangkok, Doha, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, London (Gatwick), Milan, Sharjah, and
Singapore while Chandigarh has international services to and from Dubai and Abu
Dhabi.

1603.    SHRI ASHOKRAO SHANKARRAO CHAVAN          
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether Government has prepared/proposes to prepare new 
mechanism to deal with pilot fatigue to prevent risk of air accidents 
and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether there is lots of pressure on air traffic control officials 
due to shortage of officials and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether Government is also taking steps to address staff 
shortage at the civil aviation regulator and if so, the details thereof; 
and 
 
(d) whether Government has held any meeting with official s of the 
Ministry, regulators airlines and airport operators to discuss and

Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION

promulgated Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 7, Series J, 
Part III on Flight Duty Time Limitation (FDTL), which broadly 
stipulates minimum and/maximum rest/maximum duty requirements 
of pilots to address the i ssue of stress and fatigue. The said CAR 
has been updated on 26.03.2024 to mitigate the stress and fatigue 
factor of pilots. 
 
 
 
1004                                                      

Air traffic control officers follow the regulations on watch duty time 
limitations and are properly rested before they take over  any unit to 
provide ATC services.

Sanctioned Strength     In Position     Vacant 
 
 
 
   1644*                              821             823

during 2022 to 2024.

timely and continuous availability of requisite manpower. In 
situations where the posts remain vacant due to various reasons 
like inadequat e response to the advertisements, non -joining of 
selected candidates, persons with insufficient service in the feeder 
cadre for promotion, insufficient response to deputation posts etc. 
and to meet the requirements in the interregnum, efforts are made 
to recruit persons through short terms contractual hiring.

continuous basis on various safety related issues in the civil 
aviation sector.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1607 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  4th August 2025  
INVESTIGATION AND DATA RECOVERY OF BLACK BOX 
FROM FLIGHT AI-171 CRASH 
1607.    SHRI VIVEK K. TANKHA                     
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) and Flight Data 
Recorder (FDR) from the Air India Flight AI -171 that crashed on 12th 
June, 2025, have been recovered and sent for data analysis; 
 
(b) whether the black box has been or will be sent abroad (e.g., to 
the U.S. NTSB) due to limitations in domestic labs; 
 
(c) the current status of the investigation and details of domestic or 
international collaboration in data extraction; and 
 
(d) the steps taken to enhance the country's black box decoding 
capabilities to reduce future reliance on foreign labs? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) and (b): The Flight Recorders of VT -ANB aircraft have been 
recovered. The data from one of the Flight Recorders of VT -ANB has 
been downloaded in the Flight Recorder Lab of the AAIB at Udaan 
Bhawan, New Delhi. The Flight Recorders have not been sent 
abroad. 
 
 
(c) and (d): A preliminary report on the accident has been publis hed 
by AAIB on 12.07.2025 and is available on their website 
www.aaib.gov.in. 
 
1010                                                      

 
The investigation is in progress to determine the probable 
cause(s)/contributory factor(s) leading to the accident. 
 
 
 
The Flight Recorder Laboratory in AAIB has the capability to 
download data from the flight recorders. However, as per the 
protocol laid down in International Civil Aviation Organization 
(ICAO) Annex 13 on "Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation", 
the assistance of State of Manufacturer/Design or other state s are 
taken, wherever necessary.

BIJU PATNAIK INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-
 
(a) whether there is a proposal to start international flights from Biju Patnaik
International Airport (BPIA), Bhubaneswar, to destinations like Dubai, Singapore,
and Bangkok under UDAN International; and
(b) if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
 
 
(a) & (b): Under the International Air Connectivity Scheme (IACS) -UDAN 4.0,
on the request from the Government of Odisha, bids on international routes
connecting Bhubaneswar were invited. Bids were received for routes connecting
Bhubaneswar to Bangkok, Abu Dhabi and Singapore from Air Asia airline.
However, the consent of the State Government of Odisha for accepting the entire
100% Viability Gap Funding (VGF) was not received, which was a prerequisite for
awarding these routes and subsequently, the bids were closed due to the expiry of
the bid validity period.

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  4th August 2025  
SHUTTING DOWN&#47;REPURPOSING UNDERPERFORMING 
AIRPORTS 
1610.    SMT JEBI MATHER HISHAM                  
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) the number of airports that have been operating at a loss, airport -wise 
details, including the total financial losses since their commissioning; 
(b) the names, locations, and investment details of airports that have  
remained entirely inoperative with zero passenger traffic since their 
establishment; 
(c) whether there are any plans to shut down or repurpose airports with 
zero or negligible flight operations, if so, details of such proposals airport -
wise; and 
(d) wheth er there is any proposal for viability gap funding or financial 
assistance for underperforming airports, if so, the details airport-wise? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri 
Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): For the Financial Ye ar 2024-25, a total of 81 airports owned and 
operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) have incurred financial 
loss. The airport -wise details, along with the cumulative losses suffered 
by these airports during the last ten years (FY 2015 -16 to FY 2024-25), are 
at Annexure - I. The list of AAI airports that are presently non -operational 
is at Annexure-II. 
 
(c) & (d): Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) launched Regional Connectivity 
Scheme - Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (RCS -UDAN) on 21.10.2016 to enhance 
regional air connectivity from unserved and underserved airports in the 
country. The scheme provides Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to airlines to 
bridge the gap between operational costs and expected revenues. The 
budget allocated for the RCS -UDAN for the fina ncial year 2025 -26 is 
Rs.300 crore. This scheme also provides financial incentives and 
concessions to the airlines from the Central and State Governments, 
1014                                                      

Union Territories, and airport operators to lower operational costs and 
thus promote operations from unserved and underserved airports in the 
country. 
 
RCS-UDAN is an ongoing scheme wherein bidding rounds are conducted 
from time to time for covering more destinations and routes under the 
scheme. Revival / up -gradation of unserved and underserved airports is 
undertaken upon its identification through valid bid and award to the 
Selected Airline Operator (SAO). 
 
Since the commencement of the scheme, 92 unserved and underserved 
airports, including 15 heliports and 2 water aerodromes, have been 
operationalised across the country.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1611 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  4th August 2025  
AIR SAFETY REFORMS IN THE AFTERMATH OF THE 
AHMEDABAD AIR CRASH 
1611.    DR. SASMIT PATRA                        
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) preliminary findings that have emerged from the investigation 
into the Ahmedabad air crash, and whether they have identified any 
systemic failures in air traffic control or airline protocol; 
 
(b) whether  the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has 
issued any urgent advisories or Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) 
changes post-incident; and 
 
(c) the steps that are being taken to enhance oversight of airline 
safety practices, particularly concernin g pilot fatigue, aircraft 
maintenance, and emergency response preparedness? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): A Preliminary report based on the available factual information 
has been published by Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) 
and is available on AAIB website at www.aaib.gov.in. The 
preliminary report does not contain any conclusion and 
investigation is still under progress. 
 
 
 
(b) & (c) : The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGC A) has a 
structured surveillance and audit framework in place i.e. planned 
and unplanned surveillance of organisation /aircraft, which includes 
1020                                                      

regular and periodic audits, spot checks, night surveillance and 
ramp inspections across all operators, maintenance organizations.  
 
 
DGCA continuously reviews and updates its surveillance 
methodology based on risk assessment, operator performance, fleet 
performance and global best practices such as the guidelines 
issued by European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EAS A) and 
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).  
 
 
 
DGCA issued General Safety Circular 01 of 2025 on June 19, 2025, 
titled "Comprehensive Special Audit to Assess the Aviation 
Ecosystem and Strengthen Aviation Safety Architecture". 
 
 
Regarding pilot fatigue, the new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) 
Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) provisions have come into effect. 
Monsoon checks are also being done for the operators. 
 
 
 
DGCA mandates requirements to develop & establish Aerodrome 
Emergency Plan vide DGCA CAR Section 4, Series B, Part 1, Para 9.1 
for all licensed airports to prepare an aerodrome to cope with an 
emergency occurring at the aerodrome or its vicinity. These plans 
are tested periodically and updated on the basis of 
recommendations received as out come of any case study or 
Accident/Incident report.

accommodate larger aircraft, ensure safer operations in all weather conditions and
also to initiate direct flight services to Ahmedabad and Mumbai, if so the details
thereof; and

of State will get at least one helicopter emergency medical services in the State of
Himachal Pradesh?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)

(RCS-UDAN), 32 RCS routes connecting 4 airports / heliports namely Shimla,
Kullu, Rampur (H) and Mandi (H) have been operationalised in the State of
Himachal Pradesh.
 
The Government has recently announced the modified UDAN Scheme to increase
regional connectivity to 120 new destinations across the country including
Himachal Pradesh and to cater to 4 crore passengers in the next 10 years. The
scheme will also support helipads and smaller airports in hilly, aspirational and
North East region districts.

Authority of India(AAI) has prepared a proposal for the expansion of the existing

type of aircraft under Instrument Flight Rules(IFR) conditions. The expansion and
1612. DR. SIKANDER KUMAR
1022                                                      

development of airport depends upon the availability of land, financial viability
and as well as other facilities related to intended aircraft operations.
 
With the repeal of the Air Corporation Act in March 1994, Indian domestic
aviation has been fully deregulated. Airlines are free to select markets and routes,
induct any aircraft type, and operate in compliance with the Routes Dispersal
Guidelines (RDG) issued by the government. Therefore, the decision to introduce
air services by any airline to or from any airport including Gaggal depends on the
operational and commercial viability.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO : 1614
(TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4th August 2025)
 
OBJECTIVES OF WINGS INDIA 2026
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-
 
(a) the objectives of Wings India 2026;
(b) whether advanced air mobility projects have received any regulatory, funding or pilot
project support under Wings India 2026; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
 
 
(a) : Wings India 2026 is Asia's largest civil aviation event, connecting global
stakeholders through exhibitions and high-level dialogues. The key objectives of the
event are:
i)  To showcase India's civil aviation growth and investment opportunities in the aviation
ecosystem.
ii) To facilitate collaboration among global airlines, Original equipment manufacturer
(OEMs), infrastructure providers, investors, and technology leaders.
iii) To promote innovation in safety, sustainability, Advanced Air Mobility, and digital
aviation.
iv) To enable partnerships via Government to Government(G2G)/Business to
Business(B2B)/Business to Government(B2G) meetings, roundtable conferences, and
panel discussions.
v) To support Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives by highlighting
domestic capabilities.
vi) To foster knowledge sharing and growth through conferences, technical sessions, and
engagement with youth.
 
(b) & (c):  Wings India acts as a platform for collaboration between the aviation industry
and both central and state governments, focusing on idea exchange and ecosystem
development for the civil aviation sector, including Advanced Air Mobility (AAM),
Drones, Electric Vertical Take-off and Landing aircrafts (eVTOLs) etc. As witnessed in
1614. SHRI NARHARI AMIN
SMT KIRAN CHOUDHRY
1029                                                      

previous editions, industry participation cutting across the entire spectrum of civil
aviation is expected from around the world. Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) projects are
promoted through dedicated sessions, policy roundtables, and demonstration
opportunities during the event.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO : 1616
(TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4th August 2025)
IMPACT ASSESMENT OF KRISHI UDAN SCHEME
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-
(a) whether Government has conducted any comprehensive impact assessment of
the Krishi UDAN Scheme since its inception;
(b) if so, the details thereof including its effectiveness in reducing post-harvest
losses and improving farmer income;
(c) whether there are any plans to expand the scheme to include more perishable
commodities and additional regions; and
(d) the reasons for the absence of a dedicated budget for the scheme?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
(a) & (b) The Krishi Udan Scheme is a convergence scheme where eight
Ministries/Departments namely Ministry of Civil Aviation, Department of
Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying,
Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Department of
Commerce, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Development of North-Eastern
Region leverage their existing schemes to strengthen the logistics for transportation
of Agri-produce. The Scheme aims to ensure seamless, cost effective, time-bound
air transportation and associated logistics for all Agri-produce originating
especially from Northeast, hilly and tribal regions of the country, so that it
improves their value realisation.At present, cold storage facilities are available at
35 airports across India.
(c) Krishi Udan is an ongoing Scheme and is reviewed from time to time in
consultation with stakeholders. The Scheme covers all perishable commodities,
including horticultural produce, fishery, livestock, and processed products.
(d) The Krishi Udan Scheme seeks to converge various initiatives by eight
Ministries. It has no budgetary allocation.
