& net zero emission in a phased manner. Airports are participating in Airport
Carbon Accreditation (ACA) programme of Airports Council International (ACI),
which is a voluntary global carbon management standard for airports. Bengaluru
Airport has achieved the highest Carbon Accreditation Level 5 of Airports Council
International (ACI), whereas Airports viz. Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad have
achieved Level 4+ ACI accreditation. These airports have become Carbon neutral.
 
(b) Renewable Energy (RE) sources help in reducing Carbon emissions at airports,
thereby helping in achieving carbon neutrality.  The airport operators including
Airports Authority of India (AAI) have installed solar power plants for generation
and self-consumption of green and renewable energy to encourage green energy
usage at the airports. In addition, few airports are also procuring green energy
through open access.
 
(c) The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG) has informed that Public
Sector Oil companies are engaged in setting up pilot/commercial scale facilities to
produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) including standalone as well as co-
1619. SHRI MILIND MURLI DEORA
1038                                                      

processing plants. The Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1%
by 2027, 2% by 2028, and 5% by 2030 for SAF in Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF),
initially for international flights.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1620 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  4th August 2025  
REGULATION OF AIRFARE AND AIR TARIFFS 
1620.    SHRI MEDA RAGHUNADHA REDDY               
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether Government intends to define reasonable profit as 
specified under "The Aircraft Rules, 1937" in order to curb the 
excess fares charged by airlines; 
 
(b) whether Government intends to empower the Directorate 
General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to regulate airfare; 
 
(c) whether Government intends to set up an independent body for 
monitoring airfares on the lines of Securities and Exchange Board of 
India; 
 
(d) whether Government plans to introduce a policy for uniform 
fees/tariffs across all domestic airports; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): As per Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937, every air 
transport undertaking shall establi sh a tariff having regard to all 
relevant factors, including the cost of operation, characteristics of 
service, reasonable profit, and the generally prevailing tariff. 
 
 
 
In order to enhance the transparency in airfare, Directorate General 
of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has set-up Tariff Monitoring Unit (TMU) that 
1040                                                      

monitors airfares on selected 78 routes on a random basis by using 
airlines websites on monthly basis to ensure that the airlines do not 
charge airfares outside the range declared by them, under the 
provision of sub-rule (2) of Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937. This 
covers about 27% of the domestic traffic. 
 
 
 
 
Airfares are not subject to regulation by the Government and 
airlines have the flexibility to determine their airfares based on their 
operational needs, while adhering to Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 
1937. The pricing of airfares is subject to dynamic fluctuations 
influenced by the fundamental economic forces of supply and 
demand. Various determinants such as current seat occupancy, f uel 
costs, aircraft capacity, and competitive factors significantly 
impact airline ticket pricing. 
 
 
 
To ease surge in air fare, Ministry remains vigilant and sensitize 
airlines to exercise moderation/ self - regulation, measures like 
increase in the number  of flights, reallocating capacity, etc. are 
adopted as done during Pandemic, festivals, Mahakumb and 
Pahalgam Incident. 
 
 
Given the complex dynamics of the Indian aviation industry, 
Government is playing the role of a facilitator by way of creating 
enabling environment to support the growth of the sector.

CHANGE IN THE CODE NAME OF THE GAYA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the IATA code of the International Airport in Gaya district of
Bihar is GAY, which people consider socially and culturally offensive and
uncomfortable;
(b) whether Government has been made aware of any complaints, suggestions or public
sentiments in this regard, if so, the response or discussion by Government on the same;
and
(c) whether Government is considering to change the code name GAY to a more
respectful and culturally appropriate code, if not, the reasons therefor, and if so, the
current status of this process and the likely timeline thereof?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
 
 
(a) to (c): The three-letter airport codes, also known as IATA location identifiers, are
assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) to facilitate
identification of airports across various travel-related systems and processes. These
codes are generally assigned using the first three letters of the location's name where the
airport is situated.
 
Requests for changing the code of Gaya have been received in the past by the Ministry
of Civil Aviation and Airports Authority of India.
 
IATA location codes are primarily intended for commercial airline operations and are
issued at the request of airline operators. Air India had earlier approached IATA seeking
change of the existing airport code. However, IATA has conveyed that under the
provisions of IATA Resolution 763, assigned three-letter codes are considered
permanent and are altered only under exceptional circumstances, usually involving air
safety concerns.

DEVELOPMENT OF CIVIL AVIATION INFRASTRUCTURE
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-

these projects?
 
ANSWER
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
 
 (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
 
 
(a) & (b): Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) launched Regional Connectivity
Scheme - Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (RCS-UDAN) on 21.10.2016 to enhance
regional air connectivity from unserved and underserved airports in the country
and make air travel affordable to the masses. Since the commencement of the
scheme, 92 unserved and underserved airports, including 15 heliports and 2 water
aerodromes, have been operationalised across the country.
 
RCS-UDAN is an ongoing scheme wherein bidding rounds are conducted from
time to time for covering more destinations and routes under the scheme. Revival /
up-gradation of unserved and underserved airports is undertaken upon its
identification through valid bid and award to the Selected Airline Operator (SAO).
 
The airport infrastructure development is a continuous process undertaken from
time to time depending upon the passenger demand forecast, safety of aircraft
operations, demand from airlines, availability of land and financial viability.
 
(c): The budget allocated for the RCS-UDAN for the financial year 2025-26 is
Rs.300 crore.

for RCS-UDAN projects, including periodic progress reports from implementing
agencies and airlines, regular review meetings with key stakeholders, and field
visits by AAI and State officials to track progress and address implementation
issues.

PROMOTING PRODUCTION AND USUAGE OF SUSTAINABLE

Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:-

Aviation (CORSIA) to reduce carbon emissions from international aviation. India,

The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG) has informed that Public

produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) including standalone as well as co-

by 2027, 2% by 2028, and 5% by 2030 for SAF in ATF, initially for international

stakeholders including the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, to facilitate the
development of a robust SAF ecosystem in the country.

ANSWER

(Shri Murlidhar Mohol)

Service Quality Survey (ASQ) conducted by  Airport Council 
International (ACI). The score and rankin g obtained by airports 
operated by Airports Authority of India (AAI) and partners under 
Public Private Partnership (PPP) in the ASQ Survey in their 
respective categories during 2024 is at Annexure. 
 
The performance of AAI airports with airports under PPP i s 
compared based on the average score achieved in the calendar

1051                                                      

(c): Currently, seven airports of AAI viz. Mu mbai, Lucknow,

substantially higher in comparison to AAI Airports. Hence, UDF 
levied at JV/PPP/Leased ai rports is typically higher due to 
incurrence of substantially more CAPEX. However, the aeronautical 
tariffs stabilize with increased passenger traffic over time.

ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION

is to be introduced at airports across country in a phased manner. 
The list of airports covered by DigiYatra is at Annexure. To provide 
proper data security in DigiYatra, by design/default, there is no 
central storage of passenger 's Personally Identifiable Information 
(PII) data. All the  passenger data is encrypted and stored in the 
passenger's smartphone wallet and shared only for a limited time 
duration with the origin airport where passenger ID needs to be 
validated. The data is purged from the system within 24 hours of the 
departure of the flight. A comprehensive Indian Computer 
1059                                                      

Emergency Response Team (CERT -In) Audit of DigiYatra Central 
Ecosystem has been conducted. It was established in the audit that 
DigiYatra ensures compl iance to all the industry best practices for 
data privacy, security and governance.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COAL 
  
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1633 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 04.08.2025 
  
Fatal accident at Kottadih Colliery, Paschim Bardhaman   
  
1633  Shri Ritabrata Banerjee:        
  
Will the Minister of Coal be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether it is a fact that a fatal accident occurred in Kottadih colliery (Paschim Bardhaman) 
in the recent past due to inadequate safety enforcement in Eastern Coalfields; 
  
(b) if so, the details thereof; and  
  
(c) remedial measures adopted to stop the menace of such incidents?   
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF COAL & MINES 
(SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
  
(a) & (b): The fatal accident in Kottadih colliery (Paschim Bardhaman) occurred on 03.01.2025 
and the same was inquired into by Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS). The enquiry 
report reveals that the accident did not occur due to non -compliance of safety enforcement in 
the mine.  
  
(c):  DGMS issued a safety alert t o sensitize stakeholders and reinforce preventive measures 
across mining operations immediately after the fatal accident at Kottadih Colliery on 
03.01.2025. 
  
The Central Government has enacted the Mines Act, 1952 to ensure occupational safety & 
health of mine workers, including coal mines. The Directorate General of Mines Safety 
(DGMS) has been entrusted with the task of inspection of mines to ensure the compliance of 
the provisions of the Mines Act, 1952, and rules and regulations framed thereunder for 
enhancing the safety of mine workers. Accordingly, DGMS has taken various steps to reduce 
the fatalities in mines and enforce the safety of workers engaged therein, which inter alia 
include conducting regular enquires into the accidents and dangerous occurrences to ascertain 
cause and circumstances, regular inspection of mines, development of standard protocols, 
holding national conferences on safety in mines, observance of safety weeks, campaigns, 
awareness etc.  
1068                                                      

  ECL has undertaken the following Proactive Remedial Measures to prevent recurrence of 
such incidents: - 
1. Personal Counseling:  Regular personal counseling sessions are conducted at every 
mine for employees aged 45 years and above, including both departmental and 
contractual staff, aimed at assessing personal behavior and detecting any suicidal 
tendencies. Medical officers at both the Unit and Area levels actively participate in 
these counseling efforts. 
2. Safety Counseling: A mandatory annual safety counseling programme is implemented 
in all mines to evaluate and reinforce the safety mindset of every employee, promoting 
adherence to safety norms and fostering a culture of vigilance. 
3. Family Counseling : Recognizing that safety begins at home, family counseling 
sessions are conducted for all employees to as sess their mental well-being, adherence 
to prescribed medications, and socioeconomic conditions, including debt status, thereby 
ensuring holistic support for the workforce.

environment monitoring.

specific to individual mines on the basis of identified hazards for mitigating the risk 
through control measures.

COAL BLOCKS IN ECO-SENSITIVE ZONES 
  
1635 SMT. RANJEET RANJAN: 
                         
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the coal blocks auctioned by Government since 2014 are located in 
eco-sensitive zones, forest areas, or wildlife corridors; 
(b) if so, the number and names of such blocks, and whe ther environmental and forest 
clearances were obtained prior to allocation; 
(c) whether Government has considered the long -term ecological risks and biodiversity loss 
associated with mining in such regions, and whether any blocks were withdrawn from auction 
on these ground; and 
(d) whether Government is working in consultation with other departments to balance coal 
extraction targets with India's clean energy transition goals? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF COAL & MINES  
(SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
  
(a) & (b) None of the coal blocks auctioned by the Government since 2014 are located within 
notified Eco-Sensitive Zones or Wildlife Corridors. However, several of the auctioned coal 
blocks fall within areas having forest cover. A list of auctioned coal blocks is enclos ed at 
Annexure - I.  
  Further, it is to state that the responsibility to obtain all necessary statutory clearances, 
including Environmental Clearance (EC) and Forest Clearance (FC), lies with the allocattee 
after the allocation of the coal block. However,  in accordance with the provisions of the Coal 
Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, clearances (including EC and FC), if available, are 
vested in favour of the allocattee.  
(c)   Yes, the Government undertakes a comprehensive evaluation of long-term ecological risks 
and potential biodiversity loss before permitting mining operations in sensitive areas. Further, 
in some cases coal blocks have been withdrawn from the auction process on these grounds.

Departments, including the Ministry of Power, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy 
(MNRE), NITI Aayog, and Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), 
to ensure a balanced approach towards energy security and clean energy transition.

 (c)  the number of rickshaw pullers trained or assisted under electric vehicle transition schemes; 
 
 (d)  the steps taken to safeguard traditional workers during urban transportation modernization? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (d): Urban Transport System is part of urban planning which is State subject. Maintenance of 
any data regarding number of active cycle rickshaw pullers including conducting survey thereof is a 
State function. This Ministry does not maintain the data of cycle rickshaw pullers in Indian cities. 
Government of India promotes electric rickshaws through their inclusion for incentives in impactful 
flagship schemes with a focus to transform manual labour driven to modern electric rickshaws. Under 
Deendayal Jan Aajeevika Yojana – Shehari (DJAY-S) launched with effect from 1
st October 2024, 
six vulnerable occupational groups namely, construction, gig, waste, care, domestic  and 
transportation workers  have been focussed . As per operational guidelines, transport workers are 
provided individual loan upto Rs 4 lakhs for buying or upgrading vehicles such as e -rickshaws, e-
autos, and battery- operated vehicles etc. Further, Faster Adoption & Manufacturing of Electric 
Vehicles II (FAME II) scheme supported 1.65 lakhs e lectric-3 wheeler which also included e -
rickshaws at a total cost  of Rs. 1,116 Cr.  Under PM E-DRIVE Scheme, there is specific focus on 
registered e-rickshaws and e-carts. An outlay of Rs. 192 Cr  has been kept to support 1.10 lakhs e -
rickshaw and e-carts fitted with advanced new generation battery technology.

1638.    SHRI A.A. RAHIM: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) amount allocated for a house under PMAY(U) in 2015, and the amount being allocated in 
2025; 
(b) whether Government has conducted or commissioned any study to assess impact of rising 
construction material costs due to inflation on the progress and affordability of housing under 
PMAY(U), if so, the details thereof; 
(c) recommendations or findings that have emerged on financial viability of completing houses 
within the current assistance norms; and 
(d) whether Central Government is ready to increase unit cost or financial assistance in light of 
the inflationary burden on beneficiaries and implementing agencies? 
 
           ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
 
(a) to (d) : Ministry  of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY-U) since 25.06.2015 with an aim to provide all weather 
pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. The 
scheme was implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), 
Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), In -Situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR) and Credit 
Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS). Government of India provides its fixed share as Central 
Assistance of ₹1.0 lakh under ISSR, ₹1.5 lakh for AHP and BLC verticals of PMAY -U. Under 
CLSS vertical of PMAY-U, an interest subsidy was provided for beneficiaries of Economically 
Weaker Sections (EWS)/Low Income Group (LIG) and Middle  Income Group (MIG) category 
on home loan through Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) . The remaining cost of the house as per 
DPR is shared by States/UTs/Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/Beneficiaries. Under PMAY -U, the 
State share was not mandatory however, States were providing their share as per their State 
policies.  
 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA has 
revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 
01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas across the country to support  1 crore additional 
eligible beneficiaries in next five years. PMAY -U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals 
i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), 
Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).

IMPROVEMENT IN LAST MILE CONNECTIVITY 
 
1639.            SMT. MAYA NAROLIYA 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state : 
(a) whether Government has taken necessary steps to strengthen public transport across  
            the country, with special emphasis on improving last mile connectivity;  
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and   
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (c) ‘Urban planning’ is a State  subject. Therefore, the respective State Governments are 
responsible for planning, initiating and developing proposal for development of urban infrastructure 
metro project s. Central Government provides  financial assistance to Metro Rail p roject in 
accordance with the provisions of the Metro Rail Policy, 2017 as and when posed by the  State 
Government depending on the feasibility of the proposal and availability of resources.  At present, 
about 1036 km of metro rail network including RRTS is operational in 24 cities across the country. 
Since June 2024, Government of India has sanctioned Metro Projects costing more than Rs. 1 lakh 
crore for construction of almost 240 kms of metro network. As per Metro Rail Policy  2017, last 
mile connectivity or feeder  services are to be provided by the State Government. Central 
Government has launched P M-eBus Sewa in August 2023 with an objective to increase modal 
share of public transport including support for development of e -bus ecosystem which also 
improves last mile connectivity.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1640 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
VERTICALS UNDER PMAY (U) IN SCHEDULE TRIBE AREAS 
 
1640.     DR. SUMER SINGH SOLANKI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of four different verticals present under PMAY(U) till June, 2025; and 
(b) the progress of the scheme with respect to the number of houses sanctioned, grounded 
and completed specially in Schedule Tribe areas thereof till June 2025? 
       ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) & (b): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) since 25.06.2015 with an aim to provide all 
weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities to all eligible urban beneficiaries across 
the country.  The scheme was implemented through available four verticals i.e., 
Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), In -Situ 
Slum Redevelopment (ISSR) and Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS). The 
beneficiaries were free to take benefit under any vertical. The scheme period has been 
extended up to 31.12.2025 to complete sanctioned houses without changing the funding 
pattern and implementation methodology.  
 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA 
has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with 
effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas across the country to support  1 
crore additional eligible beneficiaries in next five years. PMAY -U 2.0 is implemented 
through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in 
Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme 
(ISS). The BLC, AHP and ARH verticals of the scheme are implemented as Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme (CSS) through States and Union Territories (UTs). The ISS vertical is 
implemented as a Central Sector Scheme through Central Nodal Agencies such as 
National housing Bank (NHB), State Bank of India (SBI) and Housing and Urban 
Development Corporation Ltd. (HUDCO).  
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States /UTs, a total of 119.26 lakh houses 
including 7.09 lakh under PMAY -U 2.0 have been sanctioned under PMAY -U by the 
Ministry, so far. Out of which 112.81 lakh houses have been grounded and 93.61 lakh are 
completed/delivered to the beneficiaries across the country , as on 14.07.2025 including 
Schedule Tribes. Out of the total sanction  of  the  houses  under  the  scheme,  more  than  
1.11 lakh beneficiaries belongs to Schedule Tribes in the country.

PROGRESS OF PMAY (URBAN) IN ODISHA 
 
1641.      SHRI MANAS RANJAN MANGARAJ: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)   the total number of houses sanctioned under PMAY-U in the State of Odisha; 
(b)   the number of houses completed and occupied; 
(c)   the amount disbursed so far; 
(d)   reasons for implementation delays; and 
(e)   any timeline for completing pending projects? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
 
(a)  to (e) : Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) since 25.06.2015 with an aim to provide all weather 
pucca houses with basic civic amenities to all eligible urban beneficiaries across the country 
including Odisha. The scheme period has been extended up to 31.12.2025 to complete 
sanctioned houses without changing the funding pattern and implementation methodology.  
 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA has 
revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 
01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas across the country to support 1 crore additional 
eligible beneficiaries in next five years. PMAY -U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., 
Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable 
Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). The BLC, AHP and ARH verticals 
of the scheme are implemented as Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) through States and Union 
Territories (UTs). The ISS vertical is implemented as a Central Sector Scheme through Central 
Nodal Agencies such as National housing Bank (NHB), State Bank of India (SBI) and Housing 
and Urban Development Corporation Ltd. (HUDCO). 
 
 
…2/ - 
1084                                                      

 
-2- 
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States/UTs, a total of 119.26 lakh houses including 
7.09 lakh under PMAY-U 2.0, have been sanctioned under PMAY-U by the Ministry, so far. Out 
of which 112.81 lakh houses have been grounded and 93.61 lakh are completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries across the country as on 14.07.2025. A  total of 2,15,339 houses including 11,959 
under PMAY-U 2.0, have been sanctioned in the State of Odisha , out of which 1,85,963 have 
been grounded, of which 1,64,880 are completed /delivered to the beneficiaries, as on 
14.07.2025. A total of ₹ 3,356.36 crore of Central Assistance have been sanctioned for Odisha 
under the scheme of which ₹ 2,611.01 crore has been released.  
 
PMAY-U & PMAY- U 2.0 are demand driven scheme. More than 14 lakh houses have been 
sanctioned after 01.04.2024. Selection of beneficiaries under various verticals preferred by the 
beneficiaries, formulation of projects and execution are done by States/UTs. The timeline for 
completion of houses/projects varies from State to State and it generally takes 12- 36 months in 
different verticals of the scheme and as per Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) of respective 
projects. The completion timeline for houses depends on various factors like availability of 
encumbrance free land, statutory compliances for start of construction, arrangement of funds by 
beneficiaries etc. The Ministry conducts regular reviews with the States/UTs to monitor progress 
of implementation of the scheme and expedite completion of sanctioned houses within the 
stipulated timeline.

URBAN DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES 
 
1642.     SHRI RA VI CHANDRA V ADDIRAJU: 
 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has assessed the adequacy and likely impact of urban development 
initiatives announced in Budget 2025-26, and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the criteria for selection of cities and beneficiaries under the Urban Challenge Fund and revamped 
PM SV ANidhi scheme; 
(c)  the main challenges expected in implementing these initiatives; and 
(d) the measures proposed to address these challenges and ensure improvement in urban 
infrastructure and quality of life? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) & (b):  The Government of India, in the budget for 2025-26 has announced to set up an Urban 
Challenge Fund (UCF) of ₹1 lakh crore to implement the proposals for ‘Cities as Growth Hubs’, 
‘Creative Redevelopment of Cities’ and ‘Water and Sanitation’. As per the budget announcement, 
this fund is planned to finance up to 25 per cent of the cost of bankable projects with a stipulation 
that at least 50 per cent of the cost is funded from bonds, bank loans, and Public Private Partnerships 
(PPPs). ₹10,000 crore has been allocated for the financial year 2025- 26. Enhanced urban resilience 
and economic productivity through integrated urban planning, land -use efficiency, and sustainable 
financing are the likely impact of these initiatives. The revamping of Prime Minister Street Vendor’s 
AtmaNirbhar Nidhi Scheme (PM SV ANidhi) scheme has not been approved yet. 
 
(c) & (d): The main challenges in implementing urban development initiatives  include 
variability in the technical and administrative capacity of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), under -
utilisation of allocated funds and delays in project implementation. 
  
To address these challenges, the Government has adopted a multi-pronged approach. Capacity 
building programmes such as the National Urban Learning Platform (NULP) and iGOT have been 
launched to strengthen institutional and individual capacities at the city and S tate/ Union Territories 
(UTs) levels. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), in association with 4 Centers 
of Excellence (CoEs) in Urban Planning and Design, has launched ‘Urban Renaissance Tech Program 
for Urban Managers’ on 17 July, 2025. This program aims to develop urban managers with essential 
technical and managerial skills in implementation of urban initiatives including infrastructure, 
planning, finance and climate resilience.

SEWAGE AND WASTE MANAGEMENT IN CITIES 
 
 
1643. SHRI DHANANJAY BHIMRAO MAHADIK: 
 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether most urban local bodies have adequate sewage treatment and solid waste management 
systems in place; 
(b) the number of cities still lacking functional sewage treatment plants; 
(c) the support extended by the Central Government to such municipalities; and 
(d) whether Government is monitoring compliance with Swachh Bharat Mission targets and if any 
penalties are imposed on defaulters? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (c) :  Sanitation is a State subject under 7th schedule of the C onstitution and by the 74th 
amendment of the Constitution of India the devolution of power has been made to the Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs) for water and sanitation services. It is the responsibility of State/ULBs to plan, design, 
execute and operate sanitation projects in the urban areas of the country. Ministry of Housing & Urban 
Affairs (MoHUA) supplements the efforts of States/UTs by providing policy directions, financial and 
technical support by sharing Manuals/Standard of Procedures (SoPs) on Solid Waste Management 
(SWM) & Used Water Management (UWM) and issue various Advisories & Guidelines time to time 
for choosing appropriate technologies to manage solid and liquid waste.  
 
To support Urban Local Bodies  (ULBs) with adequate sanitation and solid waste management 
systems, Government launched the Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U) on October 2, 2014 and 
the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) in 500 cities on June 25, 
2015.  
 
To carry forward the work done on ground in Phase -I, Swachh Bharat Mission- Urban (SBM-U) 
2.0 was launched on October 1
st, 2021 for a period of five years, up to October 1, 2026, with a vision 
of achieving safe sanitation and scientific processing of municipal solid waste in all cities. 
 
As reported by States/UTs, out of total 1,61,162 ton per day (TPD) of waste generated in the 
country, 1,28,841 TPD (80%) waste is processed. Under  SWM component of SBM -U, CS assistance 
is admissible for setting up solid waste processing facilities such as Waste-to-Compost (WtC), Waste-
to-Energy (WtE), Material Recovery Facility (MRF), Construction & Demolition Waste processing 
plants, bio- methanation plants, transfer stations etc. Sanitary scientific landfills & remediation of 
legacy dumpsites etc.  
 
AMRUT 2.0 was also launched on 1 st October 2021 to make cities ‘self -reliant’ and ‘water 
secure’. Providing universal coverage of sewerage & septage management in 500 AMRUT cities 
through 2.64 crore new sewer connections/coverage with septage management is one of the major 
focus areas of AMRUT 2.0. Under AMRUT, 890 sewerage and septage management projects worth 
₹34,446.64 crore having 4,622 MLD sewage treatment capacity (new/augmented) have been grounded 
by the States / UTs. Under AMRUT 2.0, 586 sewerage/septage projects of the States/ UTs worth 
₹68,461.77 crore having 6,964 MLD sewage treatment capacity (new/augmented) have been approved  
so far. 
…2/ - 
 
1087                                                      

-2- 
 
Against 52,644 MLD of Used water generated in the country, the existing treatment capacity is 
31,885 MLD. Central Share (CS) assistance under UWM component of SBM -U 2.0 is allowed for 
cities with less than 1 lakh population for setting up of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)/Faecal Sludge 
Treatment Plants (FSTPs), Interception & Diversion (I&D) drains networks and procurement of 
mechanical desludging vehicles for safe sanitation.  
 
(d) :  Monitoring of implementation of projects under  Swachh Bharat Mission -Urban is undertaken 
through regular meeting with the state officials and assessment by video conferences, A 
comprehensive platform i.e. Swachhatam Portal has been developed which allows ULBs to create city 
profiles, upload details of city infrastructure and assets under SWM and UWM components and report 
their sanitation and waste management progress  on a monthly/periodic basis . Additionally, the 
‘Swachh Survekshan’ survey is conducted annually through third party assessment to evaluate the 
cleanliness status and progress in implementation of SBM-U in cities. The progress made in sanitation 
and management of municipal solid waste by the States/ UTs under SBM -U is regularly assessed 
through Standard Operating Protocols (SOPs) developed for certification of ULBs as Open Defecation 
Free (ODF), ODF+, ODF++ and Star ratings of Garbage Free Cities (GFC).  Further, physical and 
financial progress under the various components is duly examined before the release of next tranche of 
financial assistance to the States/UTs.

ILLEGAL WATER TANKERS AND GROUNDWATER REGULATION 
VIOLATIONS IN DELHI 
 
1645.  MS. SWATI MALIWAL: 
 
         Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government is aware of illegal water tanker mafias  operating in Delhi 
especially Sangam Vihar and Devli  village, if so , the number of cases and complaints 
reported during  the last five years, year-wise, and FIR filed; 
(b) the number of complaints regarding misuse or encroachment of Delhi Jal Board-
authorised borewells, and steps taken; 
(c) the estimated volume of groundwater extracted by private tankers in Delhi and basis of 
such estimation; and 
(d) the number of inspections conducted under Central Ground Water Authority guidelines 
and violations  found related to NOCs, digital flow meters, tanker  labelling, and BIS 
water norms? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) & ( b): The subject matter of supply of water in Delhi comes under the purview of State 
Government i.e. the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD)  and Delhi 
Jal Board (DJB) under GNCTD is the nodal Department for water supply network of drinking, 
domestic, industrial and commercial water in Delhi. 
DJB has informed that i n Sangam Vihar and De oli area, the p otable water is being supplied 
through 90-100 hired water tankers and 19 departmental water tankers.  Some complaints were 
received regarding diversion of water tankers from public to private use. In all such cases, 
penalty was imposed on the tankers and on repetitive violation, disengagement of tanker are 
also done. In the current financial year, till date, the penalty amounting to Rs. 10.50 lacs has 
been imposed on 30 water tankers and one tanker has been disengaged for repetitive violation. 
DJB has further informed that some complaints were received about misuse of DJB  bore wells 
or distribution of bore well water through private operators  in Sangam Vihar and Deoli  areas. 
DJB is ensuring that its bore well water should not be used by pri vate operators and 
distributors and that  there should be no external control on DJB bore wells. Recently, a bore 
well in F-2 Block, Sangam Vihar was taken out from the control of unauthorized person with 
the help of Police. DJB  is also engaging sufficient man power for maintaining the distribution 
network of DJB bore wells in Sangam Vihar. 
 
(c) DJB has informed that no such record is available with them with respect to the estimated 
volume of groundwater extracted by private tankers in Delhi.  
             (d)  DJB has informed that t he guideline issued by the C entral Ground Water Authority (CGWA) 
in the year 2020 and amended in the year 2023 to regulate and control groundwater extraction 
in India has not yet been implemented by GNCTD in Delhi.

(b)  the details of the ongoing projects under SCM in the State of Punjab; 
(c)     the details of the project proposals received by the Ministry under Amrut 2.0 from the State of 
Punjab and list of projects approved along with their financial outlay; and 
(d)     water treatment capacity and sewage water treatment capacity achieved in Punjab under AMRUT 
and AMRUT 2.0 so far in the State of Punjab? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a)     & (b) Under the Smart Cities Mission (SCM), three cities, viz., Amritsar, Jalandhar and Ludhiana 
have been selected from the State of Punjab. As on 31.07.2025, Punjab has taken up a total of 204 
projects amounting to ₹ 4,486 Cr under SCM. Out of this, 189 projects (93% of total projects) 
amounting to ₹4,143 Cr have been completed and the remaining 15 projects amounting to ₹342 Cr 
are ongoing. City-wise details of the completed and ongoing projects selected under SCM in the 
State of Punjab are at the Annexure-I.  
 
(c)     Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)   & AMRUT 2.0, 
States/ Union Territories (UTs) have been empowered to select appraise, propose and implement 
projects. State Level Technical Committee (SLTC) headed by the Secretary, Urban Development 
& Housing Department provides technical support to the State High Powered Steering Committee 
(SHPSC) headed by the Chief Secretary of the State, to approve, monitor and supervise the 
implementation of the scheme at the State/ UT level. On reco mmendation of the SHPSC, Apex 
Committee of Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) approves projects within the broad 
framework of Mission. 
 
 Under AMRUT 2.0, a total of 211 projects amounting to ₹3,622  Cr, submitted by the State , has 
been approved by MoHUA. Approved projects include 152 water supply projects amounting to 
₹2,980 Cr, 12 sewerage and septage management projects amounting to ₹542 Cr, 23 parks and 
green spaces projects amounting to ₹36 Cr and 24 water body rejuvenation projects amounting to 
₹63 Cr. List of projects along with the project cost is at Annexure-II. 
 
(d) In Punjab, 62 sewerage/ septage management projects amounting to ₹1,504 Cr have been taken up 
covering development/ rehabilitation of 1034.25 MLD sewage treatment plant capacity under 
AMRUT. Under AMRUT 2.0, 12 sewerage/septage management projects amounting to ₹541.86 
Cr have been approved by MoHUA in Punjab. Approved projects cover development/ 
rehabilitation of 104.90 MLD sewage treatment plant capacity.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1648 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
LEVERAGING IIT RESEARCH FOR URBAN GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE IN MAHARASHTRA  
 
1648.     SHRI SANJAY RAUT: 
 
 Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Central Government will integrate research and innovations from IITs —particularly IIT 
Bombay and other premier institutes—in the design and implementation of electric BRT systems, solar 
rooftop programs, and green buildings under the Smart Citi es Mission (SCM), especially in cities like 
Mumbai, Pune, and Nagpur; and 
 
(b) whether the Central Government has put in place any mechanism for direct technology 
transfer of low -cost, energy -efficient urban innovations to municipal bodies across  
Maharashtra and other States, to ensure that publicly funded research benefits urban 
governance, reduces emissions, and improves sustainable infrastructure delivery at the  
grassroots level? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a)     & (b) Government of India’s policy and strategy for Indian Urban Development follows the provisions 
as laid down in the Constitution of India. It is pertinent to mention here that ‘Land’ and ‘Colonization’ 
are State subjects. Further, as per the 12th Schedule of  Indian Constitution (Article 243W), Urban 
Planning including Town Planning is the responsibility of Urban Local Bodies/ Urban Development 
Authorities. Government of India supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ 
advisories.  
          Implementation of Smart Cities Mission (SCM) has been done at the City level by a Special Purpose 
Vehicle (SPV) created for planning, appraising, approving projects, releasing funds, procuring, 
managing, operating, monitoring and evaluating the Smart City development projects. Smart Cities 
Mission (SCM) followed an area-based development approach through retrofitting, redevelopment and 
greenfield development in 100 cities. The cities under SCM are being developed based on Smart City 
Proposals (SCPs) received from States/UTs , across various sectors , viz., smart mobility, Water, 
Sanitation, Hygiene (WASH), smart governance, smart energy, environment etc., approved by High 
Powered Steering Committee (HPSC).  
 With the closure of Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on March 31, 2025, there is no further budgetary 
provision under SCM to take up new projects.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1649 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
RESERVATION FOR PwDs IN CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HOUSING ALLOTMENTS 
 
1649.    DR. DINESH SHARMA: 
   SHRI BRIJ LAL:  
SHRI MITHLESH KUMAR: 
SHRI SADANAND MHALU SHET TANAVADE: 
 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the percentage of reservation proposed for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in Central 
Government housing allotments; 
 
(b) the legislative framework or policy initiative under which this reservation is implemented; 
 
(c) the operational mechanisms that have been put in place to ensure that eligible beneficiaries 
get priority in housing allocation; 
 
(d) the number of housing units estimated to be reserved across India under this policy; and  
 
(e) whether Government proposes to include accessible infrastructures real time grievance 
redressal or special housing zones in future housing masterplans for PwD?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e) : The Directorate of Estates, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, vide OM No. 
12035/9/2025-Pol.II dated 22.05.2025 has adopted reservation of 4%, as given under the Rights of 
Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, for allotment of General Pool Residential Accommodation to 
eligible Central Government servants with benchmark disabilities, as laid down in Section 34 of 
RPWD Act 2016. The OM is available at https://esampada.mohua.gov.in/signin/Circulars. 
 
A comprehensive Complaint Redressal Mechanism (CRM) has already been implemented 
within the eSampada web portal to proactively address and resolve grievances from all categories of 
users. The CRM link is https://esampada.mohua.gov.in/signin/crm.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1650 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
HERITAGE CITY DEVELOPMENT OF PURI 
 
1650.     SHRI SUBHASISH KHUNTIA:   
 
 Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Puri is included under HRIDAY or similar heritage city schemes; 
(b) the funds released for infrastructure and temple area redevelopment; 
(c) the status of Swachh Bharat Urban projects in Puri; 
(d) the timeline for completion of beautification and heritage corridor; and 
(e) the measures taken to protect architectural heritage during urban works? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): Yes, Puri city in the state of Odisha was included under the HRIDAY scheme  of Ministry of 
Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)  and is now under the Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual 
Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD Scheme) of Ministry of Tourism. 
 
(b) & (d): During the period of the HRIDAY Scheme in the MoHUA which ended on the 31 st of 
March, 2019, six projects were completed in Puri (Odisha). The details of the projects along with the 
release of funds and timeline are at Annexure-A. 
 
 Further, under PRASHAD Scheme of the Ministry of Tourism, a project titled “Infrastructure 
Development at Puri, Shree Jagannath Dham -Ramachandi-Prachi Riverfr ont at Deuli under Mega 
Circuit” was sanctioned during the Financial Year 2014-15. Rs. 10.00 Crore was released to the Project 
which was later foreclosed. The major components undertaken as part of the project were: 
 
(i) Gundicha Temple  - Landscaping, Pathways, stonework, illuminations , benches, 
Boundary Wall. 
(ii) Development at Prachi  River Front  (Drinking water facilities, Entrance Gate, Prayer 
Hall, Benches, Steps, Walkway) 
(iii) Maa Mangala Temple - Dustbins, Handpumps, Pathways, Public conveyances, Waste 
Disposal system. 
 
(c):  Details of the implementation status of Swachh Bharat Urban Projects in Puri are at Annexure-B. 
 
(e): Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana (HRIDAY), a central sector scheme, 
was launched on 21st of January, 2015. The main objective of the scheme was to preserve the character 
and the soul of heritage cities and facilitate inclusive heritage -linked urban development by exploring 
various avenues, including involving the private sector. The mission period of the HRIDAY ended on  
the 31st of March, 2019. No new cit y or project has been taken up after the 31st of March, 2019 by the 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under the scheme. On discontinuation of this scheme, the 
heritage component has been included in the National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and 
Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD Scheme), which is now being administered by the 
Ministry of Tourism.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1651 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
STATUS OF BACKLOG OF VACANCIES 
1651.  SMT. PRIYANKA CHATURVEDI: 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware of the status of backlog vacancies, which touched 774 
at the beginning of this year, as published on 1st January, 2025; 
(b) whether Government has any reasoning for the number of unfilled vacancies for SC, 
ST, and OBC; 
(c) the reasons for the numerous vacant seats and the inaction on the part of the Ministry 
to fill them; and 
(d) whether the Ministry took any subsequent measures to cover this gap, if so, the details 
thereon? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
(a) : Yes. 
(b) to (d): Occurrence and filling up of vacancies, along with backlog reserved vacancies, is a 
continuous process. The vacancies reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs)/Scheduled Tribes 
(STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) are filled up as per Government guidelines and 
man-power planning.  
MoHUA has a dedicated Reservation Cell and Deputy Secretary/Director level Liaison 
Officers to ensure due compliance of the orders and instructions pertaining to reservation in 
service. As per the directions of Department of Personnel and Training, MoHUA has also 
constituted an in- house Committee to, inter -alia, review the status of backlog reserved 
vacancies. 
As recruitment is a time -consuming process, there is generally a time -gap between 
occurrence of vacancies and filling up of such vacancies. The backlog of SC/ST/OBC 
vacancies, if any, due to non- availability of candidates or non- reporting of the selected 
candidates are included in the next year’s recruitment process.  
As reported by the Organisations under MoHUA, out of the 774 backlog reserved 
vacancies as on 01.01.2025, 124 backlog reserved vacancies have already been filled up.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1652 
ANSWERED ON  04/08/2025 
 
LOSS OF GOVERNMENT REVENUE DUE TO NON-REGISTRATION OF FLATS 
 
1652.    DR. LAXMIKANT BAJPAYEE:      
 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the cases in Noida and other cities where builders have handed over possession of 
flats after receiving full payment from buyers, but have not completed the mandatory registration of 
the flats, resulting in loss of stamp duty and registration fee revenue to Government; and  
 
(b) whether Government proposes to exercise its powers under the Concurrent List to introduce a 
central legislation making registration of flats mandatory, in order to  prevent substantial losses of 
stamp duty and registration fee and to protect the interests of flat buyers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) & (b):  ‘Land’, ‘Colonization’ and ‘Stamp Duty’ fall under the jurisdiction of State Governments, as 
per List – II (State List) of the seventh schedule of the Constitution of India. No such proposal to 
introduce a central legislation is under consideration.

1114                                                      

 
 
O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1653 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF FUNDS 
 
1653.    SMT. MAHUA MAJI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps taken by Government to ensure equitable distribution of AMRUT funds in small towns 
and tribal areas of the State of Jharkhand; and 
(b) the steps taken to implement Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) guidelines in AMRUT 
Projects in 2023-24? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) was launched on 25 
June 2015 in selected 500 cities (485 cities including 15 merged cities) and towns across the country 
including 07 cities of Jharkhand. Allocation of funds to the States/Union Territories (UTs) under 
AMRUT was done  at the beginning of the Mission, using an equitable formula giving equal 
weightage (50:50) to the urban population of each State/  UT as per Census 2011 and the number of 
statutory towns in the State/ Union Territory. Against the committed Central Assistance (CA) of 
₹566.17 crore for projects to the State of Jharkhand under AMRUT, ₹551.69 crore has been released.  
AMRUT 2.0 scheme has been launched on 01 October 2021 in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ cities 
in the country including 50 Cities/ULBs of Jharkhand. Under AMRUT 2.0, States/UTs are 
empowered to select, prioritise, design, implement and monitor the projects within the broad 
framework of Mission guidelines. 
 
(b): The projects under AMRUT/ AMRUT 2.0 are for development of basic infrastructure in urban 
areas such as water supply, sewerage and septage management, parks and green spaces, etc, which 
benefit all the people of the area. The AMRUT 2.0 guidelines promotes gender  equality and social 
inclusion. AMRUT Mitra initiative has been launched under AMRUT 2.0 to actively involve women 
Self Help Groups (SHG) in water quality testing, water infrastructure  operations and other water 
sectoral projects, which include maintenance of parks and green spaces.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1654 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
TARGET SET FOR PROVIDING HOUSES TO THE POOR PEOPLE 
 
1654.       SHRI NAVEEN JAIN: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of poor people provided houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana 
(PMAY) in the country till March 31st, 2025 and the State-wise details thereof; and 
(b) the target set for number of poor people to be provided houses in the financial years 2025 -
26, 2026-27 and 2027-28? 
         ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
 
(a)  & (b):  Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY-U) since 25.06.2015 with an aim to provide all weather 
pucca houses with basic civic amenities to all eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. 
The scheme period has been extended up to 31.12.2025 to complete sanctioned houses without 
changing the funding pattern and implementation methodology. Based on the learnings from the 
experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched 
PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in 
urban areas across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible beneficiaries in next five 
years. PMAY -U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction 
(BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and 
Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).  
 
PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 are demand driven schemes. Therefore, no specific State wise target 
are fixed for the years 2025-26, 2026-27 and 2027-28. As per the scheme guidelines, selection of 
beneficiaries, formulation of projects and execution is done by States/ Union Territories ( UTs). 
After demand assessment and verification, States/UTs prepare project proposals and after 
approval of State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC), these  are submitted 
to the Ministry for sanctioning of admissible Central Assistance by Central Sanctioning and 
Monitoring Committee (CSMC).  Moreover, conducting demand surveys  in their respective 
jurisdictions and validating the beneficiaries to ascertain eligibility by the States/UTs is a 
continuous process. Eligible citizens are also allowed to apply through Unified Web Portal of 
PMAY-U 2.0 and register their demand.  
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States/UTs, a total of 119.26 lakh houses including 
7.09 lakh under PMAY-U 2.0 have been sanctioned under PMAY-U by the Ministry, so far. Out 
of which 112.81 lakh houses have been grounded and 93.61 lakh are completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries across the country as on 14.07.2025. The State/UT -wise details of houses 
sanctioned, grounded and completed so far are at Annexure.

(c): As per 12th Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban planning including town planning is 
the function of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban Development Authorities. Government of India 
supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions / advisories. The Government 
has ensured structured professional involvement in urban development programmes  such as Smart 
Cities Mission (SCM) & Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) . In 
accordance with the guidelines of SCM, the Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) of the smart cities are 
responsible for design, implementation, and operation of smart city projects. Advisory was issued by 
MoHUA on 4th July 2016 for “Engagement of Key Managerial Posts and Human Resources in 
SPVs”. SPVs leverage this advisory for hiring of qualified professionals across various domain 
including architects, urban planners, finance professionals for fulfilling their requirements. Similarly, 
under AMRUT, State Annual Action Plans and Detailed Project Reports are required to be prepared 
by technical teams comprising qualified engineering, architects and planners, particularly for projects 
related to water supply, sanitation, urban transport, and public amenities. Further, the Government 
incentivised the States for recruitment of urban planners under SSASCI 2023-24 (Urban Planning 
Reforms). As reported by the State, 1034 vacant posts of Planners were filled (Regular/Contractual). 
 
(d): The Smart Cities Mission and AMRUT 2.0 guidelines include provisions to promote climate-
responsive and environment -friendly urban design practices. Projects under SCM are aimed at 
improving liveability, economic-ability, and sustainability. The focus is on sustainable and inclusive 
development and developing compact areas. Similarly, the AMRUT 2.0 operational guidelines focus 
on improving water security and urban resilience through measures such as rejuvenation of water 
bodies, development of green spa ces, energy-efficient water supply systems, and integrated urban 
planning that supports low -carbon growth. These provisions reflect the integration of climate -
sensitive and sustainable design principles into urban infrastructure projects.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1656 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
MANDATORY DISPLAY OF LOGO ON BENEFICIARY HOUSES UNDER PMAY (U) 
 
1656.      DR. JOHN BRITTAS:  
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the dimensions, colours, texts and images mandated in the logo insisted to be affixed 
on each house under PMAY-(U); 
(b) whether it is a fact that States including Kerala have objected to the mandatory PMAY -(U) logo 
display on beneficiary houses citing dignity, privacy, self -respect of economically weaker 
beneficiaries, and federal concerns; and 
(c) if so, whether Government will review its insistence on permanent branding on homes under PMAY-
(U), considering that safe housing is a basic right of citizens and not a gift to warrant permanent 
branding on private homes? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a):  The scheme guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) and PMAY-U 
2.0 have been prepared after a series of consultations with States/Union Territories (UTs) and a large 
number of other stakeholders. As per the PMAY- U 2.0 scheme guidelines, it is mandatory for 
States/UTs to ensure display of PMAY -Urban logo along with the details of beneficiary embossed 
or engraved thereon, preferably in local language on all houses constructed under the scheme. Display 
of logo on PMAY -U houses ensures authenti city and transparency in the implementation of the 
scheme across States/UTs. Therefore, States/UTs have been advised to keep the name of the scheme 
intact and not modify it in any manner during implementation. 
 
(b) & (c ): The branding ensures openness & transparency in selection of beneficiaries and has 
qualities of inherent social audit. All States/UTs signing Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) have 
agreed to implement the PMAY-U 2.0 as per guidelines and not sought any exemption. The State of 
Kerala is yet to sign the MoA for implementing the PMAY-U 2.0 scheme.

ADB SUPPORT FOR INDIA'S URBANIZATION AGENDA 
 
1657.     SHRI MAYANKKUMAR NAYAK: 
DR. K. LAXMAN: 
SHRI KESRIDEVSINH JHALA: 
 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a) the manner in which  the Asian Development Bank (ADB) has supported India's urbanization 
agenda in alignment with the priorities of the Union Budget 2025-26; 
(b) whether ADB has committed to any demonstration or "lighthouse" projects for future urban 
development; and 
(c) if so, the intended locations, objectives, and expected outcomes? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government of India, in the budget for 2024- 25, has announced that the 
Government will facilitate development of Cities as Growth hubs, formulate a framework  for 
enabling policies, market -based mechanisms and regulation  for Creative B rownfield 
Redevelopment of existing cities  and, promote water supply, sewage treatment and solid waste 
management projects and services for 100 large cities through bankable projects . Asian 
Development Bank (ADB) and World Bank Group have jointly developed knowledge 
frameworks for three priority areas.  
Further, the Government of India, in the budget for 2025-26 has announced to set up an Urban 
Challenge Fund (UCF) of ₹1 lakh crore to implement the proposals for ‘Cities as Growth Hubs’, 
‘Creative Redevelopment of Cities’ and ‘Water and Sanitation’. As per the budget announcement, 
this fund is planned to finance up to 25 per cent of the cost of bankable projects with a stipulation 
that at least 50 per cent of the cost is funded from bonds, bank loans, and Public Private 
Partnerships (PPPs). ₹10,000 crore ha s been allocated for the financial year 2025- 26. The 
objective is to enhance urban resilience and economic productivity through integrated urban 
planning, land-use efficiency, and sustainable financing.

KEY ACHIEVEMENTS UNDER SMART CITIES MISSION 
1658.     SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: 
 Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the progress that has been made on the Smart Cities Mission (SCM), and the manner in which 
urban infrastructure will be improved in 2025-2026; 
(b)  the key achievements Ministry has recorded for the SCM by 2025; 
(c)     which urban infrastructure projects is the Ministry prioritizing in 2025; and 
(d)   the manner in which the Ministry will assess urban infrastructure improvements by 2026?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a)    to (d): Smart Cities Mission (SCM) was launched on 25.06.2015. Implementation of SCM at the 
City level has been done by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) created for planning, appraising, 
approving projects, releasing funds, procuring, managing, operating, monitoring and evaluating 
the Smart City development projects. SCM followed an area-based development approach through 
retrofitting, redevelopment and greenfield development in 100 cities.  
 
         As per the information provided by the States/UTs, as on 31.07.2025, out of a total 8063 projects 
amounting to ₹ 1,64,695 Cr undertaken in the 100 cities selected under SCM, 7,636 projects (95% 
of total projects) amounting to ₹1,53,977 Cr have been completed and
 the remaining 427 projects 
amounting to ₹10,718 Cr are ongoing.  
          Under SCM, the Central Government had a total outlay of ₹48,000 Cr for the 100 cities. As on 
31.07.2025, the cities have been able to claim Central financial assistance of ₹47,459 Cr (i.e. 99% 
of the total Central share allocation), out of which the States/Union Territories are reported to have 
utilized ₹45,881 Cr (i.e. 97% of the total Central share claimed).  
          
 The cities under SCM are being developed based on Smart City Proposals (SCPs) received from 
States/UTs, across various sectors , viz., smart mobility, Water, Sanitation, Hygiene (WASH), 
smart governance, smart energy, environment etc., approved by High Powered Steering 
Committee (HPSC). Sector wise details of milestone achieved under SCM is at Annexure. 
 With the closure of Smart Cities Mission (SCM) on March 31, 2025, there is no further budgetary 
provision under SCM to take up new projects.

IRRIGATION, WATER BODY RESTORATION SCHEMES IN BIHAR 
1659 #.  SHRI SANJAY KUMAR JHA 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) details of irrigation projects and water bodies  restoration schemes sanctioned in the State of Bih ar 
during the last five years under Pradhan Mantri Kri shi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), Repair, Renovation 
and Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies, Har Khet Ko Pani and Jal Shakti Abhiyan, which include ponds 
(talabs), tanks and traditional systems like ahar-pyne; 
(b) number of water bodies restored, renovated pond s, length of newly constructed canals (in km) and 
newly created additional irrigated area (total hectares) in the State of Bihar; and 
(c) impact on farmers of the State of Bihar, includ ing improvement in crop yield, farmer's income, 
groundwater recharge, employment in rural areas? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) to (c)   Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Kri shi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) scheme 
in 2015-16 by consolidating several ongoing initiat ives, including the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits  
Programme (AIBP), Command Area Development & Water Management (CADWM), Surface Minor 
Irrigation (SMI), Repair, Rejuvenation & Restoratio n (RRR) of Water Bodies, Integrated Watershed 
Management Programme (IWMP), and the Micro Irrigati on component of On Farm Water Management 
(OFWM). The primary objective of PMKSY is to enhanc e physical access to water for farms, expand 
cultivable areas under assured irrigation, improve on-farm water use efficiency, and promote sustainab le 
water conservation practices. 
Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) is one of the key component s of PMKSY. The Surface Minor Irrigation 
and RRR of Water Bodies schemes were incorporated a s part of PMKSY-HKKP. Under the RRR of Water 
Bodies component of PMKSY-HKKP, Government of India  has approved a  cluster of 10 number Repair, 
Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies sc hemes of Bihar having an estimated cost of Rs. 
73.05 crore for providing the Central Assistance am ounting to Rs. 43.83 crore under the Pradhan Mantri  
Krishi Sinchayee Yojna -Har Khet Ko Pani (PMKSY-HKKP) in March 2025. The scheme aims to restore a 
1126                                                      

2 
 
Irrigation Potential (IP) of 5,477 hectares and rev ive water storage capacity of 3.187 million cubic m eters 
(MCM).  
Further, under the PMKSY-AIBP,  one project, namely  the Koshi-Mechi Intra-state River Link 
Project, pertaining to Bihar  having an estimated c ost of Rs. 6282.32 crore  and targeted irrigation 
Potenential of 2.15 lakh hactare  has been included in March 2025. 
The Ministry of Jal Shakti has also been implementi ng the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: 
CTR) initiative, focusing on five key areas: water conservation and rainwater harvesting, reuse and 
recharge structures, watershed development, intensi ve afforestation, and renovation of traditional wat er 
bodies. Under the JSA: CTR initiative, a total of 3 0,142 traditional water bodies in Bihar were renova ted 
during the JSA years 2021 to 2025.  
To strengthen JSA: CTR, "Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari"  (JSJB) initiative, launched in Surat, Gujarat 
on 6th September 2024, focuses on intensifying comm unity action and mobilization to build low cost 
rainwater harvesting structures in low cost and sat uration mode.  Under the JSJB initative, a total  1 33891 
works related to ground water recharge and storage works  have been completed in Bihar up to 31st May 
2025.

resources in respect of Bihar exhibited enhanced re charge of 2.74 BCM in the Year 2024 as compared to

State authorities in rejuvenating groundwater and natural water resources.

WATER CRISIS AFFECTED DISTRICTS IN THE COUNTRY 
1660 #.   MS. INDU BALA GOSWAMI 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has identified water-crisis affected districts across the country; 
(b) if so, the number of such Districts, State-wise details thereof; 
(c) whether any team has been constituted by Govern ment to review the implementation of Jal Shakti 
Abhiyan Schemes; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) & (b)  Water, being a State subject, places the primary re sponsibility for the augmentation, 
conservation, assessment and efficient management o f water resources with the respective State 
Governments. However, the Central Government supple ments the efforts of the States through technical 
and financial support. 
  The Ministry of Jal Shakti launched the Jal Shakt i Abhiyan (JSA) in 2019 as a time-bound, 
mission-mode water conservation campaign in 256 wat er-stressed districts of the country. The Hon'ble 
Prime Minister launched “Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain” (JSA: CTR) in 2021 with the tagline 
“Catch the Rain – Where it Falls When it Falls”. Th e Abhiyan was scaled up to cover all districts, 
blocks, and municipalities across the country. 
  Although JSA:CTR campaign is implemented nationwi de, each edition has included a targeted 
focus since 2023 to maximize impact. The JSA: CTR 2 023, with the theme “Source Sustainability for 
Drinking Water,” prioritized 150 special focus dist ricts identified by the Jal Jeevan Mission. The JSA : 
CTR 2024 campaign, themed “Nari Shakti se Jal Shakt i,” was carried out across the country with a 
special focus on 151 districts identified by the Ce ntral Ground Water Board (CGWB). The JSA: CTR 
2025 was launched with the theme “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or” emphasizing deeper 
grassroots engagement, inter-sectoral convergence a nd innovative financing mechanisms with special 
focus on 148 districts identified by CGWB.  The lists of focused districts under JSA:CTR Campaign (for 
2025, 2024 & 2023) is attached at Annexure I.  
1128                                                      

2 
 
   
 
Additionally, The Dynamic Ground Water Resources of  the country are assessed every year 
from 2022 jointly by Central Ground Water Board (CG WB) and State Governments to analyze trends in 
groundwater recharge and extraction. As per the rep ort of “National Compilation of Dynamic Ground 
Water Resources of India, 2024”, shared by CGWB, 10 2 districts are categorized as ‘Over- exploited’, 
22 districts are categorized as ‘Critical’ and 69 d istricts are categorized as “Semi-critical”. The St ate 
wise details of 193 OCS (Over Exploited, Critical a nd Semi Critical) districts is provided in Annexure-
II.  
(c) & (d) ‘ Water’ is State subject and the Central Government supplements the efforts of the States 
through technical and financial support. Water cons ervation is one of the foremost priorities of the 
Government.  
  To address the challenges faced by States and loc al bodies in implementing rainwater harvesting 
systems, particularly in water-stressed regions, th e Government of India has adopted a comprehensive, 
multi-pronged approach. As part of this strategy, C entral teams consisting of Central Nodal Officers 
(CNOs) of the Rank of Additional Secretary/Joint Se cretary/ Director/ Deputy Secretary and Technical 
Officers (TOs) from the organizations of DoWR, RD &  GR (CWC, CGWB, NIH, CSMRS, CWPRS, 
etc) are sent for field visits to the focused distr icts during the campaign for interaction with distr ict 
authorities on Jal Shakti Abhiyan and to facilitate  the districts and provide technical assistance. Fu rther, 
State Nodal Officers are also appointed by all the states/ UTs to oversee the implementation of the 
campaign at state level.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1661  
ANSWERED ON 04.08.2025 
FUNDS SPENT AND WATER QUALITY UNDER NGM 
1661.   DR. V. SIVADASAN 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the total amount of funds allocated, released, and spent under the Namami Gange  Mission (NGM) 
since its inception, year-wise and State-wise; 
(b) whether the water quality of the Ganga river at major locations has improved to the level of being safe 
for bathing and other direct contact activities without filtration; 
(c) the details of water quality parameters (like BOD, coliform count, pH, etc.) assessed at major stretches 
of the river during the last three years; and 
(d) whether any third -party audits or evaluations have been conducted to assess the impact  and 
effectiveness of the mission, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a)   The year-wise details of the funds allocated and the amount disbursed by the National Mission for 
Clean Ganga (NMCG) to various agencies for implementation of projects/ interventions under the 
Namami Gange Programme since its inception (Financial Year (FY)  2014-15) till 30 June 2025 are 
enclosed in Annexure I. 
No State -wise allocation is made under the Namami Gange programme. However, the amount 
disbursed to various agencies, including State Missions for Clean Ganga, under the said Programme till 
30th June 2025, compiled State-wise, is enclosed in Annexure II. 
(b) & (c)   The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has carried out water quality monitoring of the 
river Ganga. The water quality data of the river Ganga for the years 2022 to 2024 (based on median 
values) with respect to the parameters pH, DO and BOD is enclosed in Annexure-III. 
Based on the median values of water quality data for the year 2024 (January –December), the entire 
stretch of river Ganga generally conforms to the primary water quality criteria for outdoor bathing in 
terms of pH, Dissolved Oxygen (DO), and Biochemical Oxy gen Demand (BOD), except for marginal 
BOD exceedance at certain stretches in Uttar Pradesh. Faecal Coliform (median) primary water quality 
1140                                                      

2 
 
criteria for bathing is met in the entire stretch of river Ganga in Uttarakhand & Jharkhand and certain 
stretches of UP, Bihar and West Bengal while Faecal Streptococci (median) the primary water quality 
criteria for bathing is met in the entire stretch of  river Ganga in Uttarakhand, Bihar & Jharkhand and 
certain stretches of UP and West Bengal. 
(d)     Yes. The Administrative Staff College of India (ASCI) was engaged as a Third Party Agency (TPA) 
for the appraisal of the Namami Gange Mission (NGM). ASCI has observed the following in its report: 
i. NGM has led to considerable additions to wastewater treatment infrastructure in the Ganga 
river basin, balanced with investments in riverfront and ghat development, river surface 
cleaning processes, afforestation, biodiversity conservation, organic agriculture, etc. 
ii. Capacity building of implementing agencies and other stakeholders, along with community 
engagement to support the initiatives, are among the other key contributions of the projects. 
iii. The decentralisation and mainstreaming of program tasks within the basin states and local 
body establishments have been the hallmark of the programme. 
iv. ASCI, in its appraisal, stated that NGM has shown good progress in achieving its mandate of 
continuous flow (Aviral Dhara) and unpolluted flow (Nirmal Dhara). 
v. It has demonstrated successful and replicable models for implementing a large -scale river 
rejuvenation programme in a mission mode and has gained global recognition.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION 
  
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1662 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2025 
 
JAL JEEVAN MISSION 
 
1662 # SHRI RAMJI LAL SUMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the State-wise details of the complaints received under Har Ghar Jal Yojana under Jal  Jeevan 
Mission; 
 
(b) whether it is a fact that the water is not being supplied in the taps in many of the  villages 
where drinking water has been provided through pipes; and 
 
(c) the details of the funds released under this scheme so far? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
 
(a) & (b) Government of India is committed to make provision for safe & potable tap water 
supply in adequate quantity, of prescribed quality on a regular & long -term basis to all rural 
households in the country.  Towards this end, the Government of India launched the Jal Jeevan 
Mission (JJM), to be implemented in partnership with States/ UTs, in August 2019. The 
significant progress has been made under the mission as in August 2019, only 3.23 crore (16.7%) 
rural households were reported to have tap water connect ions, while as on 30.07.2025, out of 
19.36 crore rural households, more than 15.67 crore (80.9 7%) are reported to have tap water 
supply. 
 
Water is a state subject and, therefore, the primary responsibility f or planning, implementation, 
and operation & maintenance (O&M) of piped water supply schemes to provide tap water to 
rural households, lies with the respective State/UT Government. As such, grievances/ 
complaints, etc. inter alia including corruption, sub -standard work, etc. under JJM are handled 
and disposed of at the State/ UT level. Such complaints/ representations as and when received in 
this department are forwarded to the state government for taking necessary corrective measures.  
 
Department of Drink ing Water & Sanitation undertakes assessment of the functionality of 
household tap water connections provided under the mission, through an independent third-party 
agency, based on standard statistical sampling. During the Functionality Assessment 2022, it was 
found that 86% of households (HHs) had working tap connections. Out of these, 85% were 
getting water in adequate quantity, 80% were getting water regularly as per the schedule of water 
supply for their piped water supply scheme, and  87% of households were receiving water as per 
1145

the prescribed water quality standards. A copy of last Functionality Assessment 2022 is in public

at multiple levels.
